news.head: Buccaneers D/ST put in tough spot Sunday
news.body: The Buccaneers D/ST allowed 26 points on 351 total yards with one interception and one sack on Sunday against the Bengals.
news.impact: Cincinnati scored 33 points, but one of them was off a fumble by Baker Mayfield returned for a touchdown. The Bengals also scored 17 other points off Bucs fumbles. The Bucs will be on the streaming radar in Week 2 against the Browns.

news.head: Buccaneers D/ST recovers two fumbles in Week 18
news.body: The Buccaneers D/ST allowed 14 points on 285 total yards with one interception and two fumble recoveries in Week 18 against the Panthers.
news.impact: While the Bucs secondary struggled most of the season, they held their own to close the season while also completely shutting down the Panthers rushing attack. The Bucs also recovered a pair of fumbles and added an interception.

news.head: Tampa Bay Buccaneers D/ST struggles Sunday against Dolphins
news.body: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers D/ST failed to come up with any big plays on Sunday against Quinn Ewers and the Dolphins' offense on Sunday. Tampa Bay fell 20-17 to Miami, its seventh loss in the last eight games.
news.impact: The Buccaneers allowed only 298 yards of total offense and kept the Dolphins to just 4-of-12 on third-down conversions, but they failed to force a turnover and only sacked Ewers twice in the game. It's the second straight game the Buccaneers have not forced a turnover and they have only four in the last six games after registering 16 in their first 10 games. Tampa Bay has a chance for redemption when it hosts Carolina for the NFC South title on Saturday.

news.head: Tampa Bay Buccaneers D/ST quiet against Carolina
news.body: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers D/ST managed two sacks with no turnovers in the Bucs' 23-20 loss to Carolina on Sunday.
news.impact: The Bucs defense was quiet in this game aside from two sacks. To their credit, they played decently well against the surging Panthers, but fantasy managers would have loved to see more from them. They should be a good start next week against Quinn Ewers and the Dolphins.

news.head: Garrett Wilson goes for 79 yards in Week 1
news.body: Garrett Wilson caught six of his seven targets for 79 yards in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
news.impact: Wilson led the Jets in all receiving categories in the easy win over an overmatched Tennessee team. Even though it wasn't a huge performance from Wilson, it was an encouraging debut for the receiver with Geno Smith at the helm. Wilson settles in as a high-end WR2 in a Week 2 home matchup against the Packers.

news.head: Garrett Wilson (illness) back at practice Tuesday
news.body: Garrett Wilson (illness) was back in action Tuesday after missing Monday's practice.
news.impact: Nothing much to see here for Wilson. The Jets' No. 1 receiver sat out Monday due to being under the weather, but he was back on the practice field Tuesday.

news.head: Garrett Wilson (illness) not at practice Monday
news.body: Garrett Wilson (illness) did not participate in practice on Monday due to an illness.
news.impact: Thankfully, this sort of practice absence is one where it raises little, if any, concern. Wilson will likely return to practice as normal within the next day or so.

news.head: Garrett Wilson (knee) will not return this season
news.body: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Garrett Wilson will not play for the rest of the season.
news.impact: It comes as no surprise that Wilson will not return for a Jets team that has nothing to play for. He was placed on injured reserve back in the middle of November. He finishes the season having caught 36 passes for 395 yards and four touchdowns.

news.head: Josh Jacobs has court appearance date moved up
news.body: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs had his initial court appearance moved up to Sept. 10 from Nov. 17 regarding Jacobs' misdemeanor charges.
news.impact: Jacobs was charged with battery and criminal destruction of property and is scheduled to appear at the Brown County courthouse on Sept. 10, multiple days before Green Bay's season opener against Minnesota. It is unclear how this will affect his return timeline; Jacobs is currently on the commissioner's exempt list, with a potential suspension looming.

news.head: Josh Jacobs expected to play for Packers in 2026 per GM
news.body: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst said he expected Josh Jacobs to play for the team in 2026.
news.impact: Gutekunst said he wants to let the process play out when asked if there’s a scenario in which the Packers release Jacobs. He was placed on the Commissioners Exempt List on Sunday. This will remain a situation to monitor.

news.head: Josh Jacobs placed on commissioner of exempt list
news.body: Josh Jacobs has been placed on the commissioner exempt list by the National Football League according to Tom Pelissero.
news.impact: Jacobs is now ineligible to practice or play for the Packers while the league continues their investigation into alleged improper behavior while being charged with two misdemeanors related to his conduct earlier in the week. If the running back is forced to sit out for any period of the regular season, MarShawn Lloyd will be in line to receive the majority of backfield work while the recently acquired Kaleb Johnson gets up to speed on the offensive playbook with Week 1 approaching.

news.head: Josh Jacobs charged with two misdemeanors stemming from May incident
news.body: Josh Jacobs has been charged with two misdemeanors following an incident in May. His initial court date is set for mid-November. The NFL is conducting its own investigation, and a suspension could soon follow.
news.impact: It's important to remember that the NFL has the ability to either suspend Jacobs at the start of the season or wait until the legal process is over. If they wait, then Jacobs will likely not face suspension until next year. If not, we could be looking at a potential 6-8 game absence, though that is more of an educated guess at this point. For anyone taking Jacobs in drafts right now, Marshawn Lloyd is a must-have handcuff and is a great target for Zero-RB builds.

news.head: Dak Prescott underwhelming in loss Sunday
news.body: Dak Prescott completed 22-of-34 passing attempts for 175 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.impact: Prescott didn't deliver a great performance on Sunday night. He was held to under 200 passing yards against the Giants and lost one turnover in Dallas' loss to their divisional rival. He will have a good opportunity to bounce back next week against the Commanders, but this is not the type of performance fantasy managers wanted to see out of him in the season opener.

news.head: Dak Prescott, Cowboys starters will not play in preseason
news.body: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he won’t play starters in the preseason.
news.impact: Schottenheimer said he broke up all players into four groups for preseason playing time. The A group plays zero snaps, B+ group plays 10-15 snaps, B- group plays 20-25 snaps and the C group plays unlimited snaps. We'll get our first look at Dak Prescott and the Cowboys starters in Week 1 against the Giants.

news.head: Dak Prescott (knee) limited in practice Tuesday
news.body: Dak Prescott was limited in practice during minicamp on Tuesday.
news.impact: Prescott took four reps in team drills when he would normally would’ve had eight. It does not appear to be anything serious that he is dealing with after he was expected to be limited.

news.head: Dak Prescott has contract restructured by Cowboys
news.body: The Cowboys restructured the contract of Dak Prescott.
news.impact: Prescott, Tyler Smith and CeeDee Lamb all had their contracts restructured to help create a significant amount of capital space for the Cowboys. They are now under the cap heading into free agency.

news.head: Drake Maye throws three interceptions in loss Wednesday
news.body: Drake Maye completed 23-of-33 passing attempts for 178 yards, one touchdown, and three interceptions while adding 47 yards on the ground in Wednesday night's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.impact: Maye started the season on the wrong foot on Wednesday night. He threw for under 200 yards and three interceptions against a tough Seattle defense, including one that cost the Patriots the game. He still showed lots of ability on the ground, however, and he's likely to return to being a good fantasy option against easier defenses. The loss of A.J. Brown (ankle) for at least a few games will severely hamper his short-term upside, however.

news.head: Drake Maye (shoulder) off injury report for Super Bowl
news.body: Drake Maye is not on the injury report for the Super Bowl against the Seahawks.
news.impact: Maye was able to practice fully all week. He is officially good to go for the biggest game of the season on Sunday.

news.head: Drake Maye (shoulder) logs full practice Thursday
news.body: Drake Maye was a full participant in practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Maye has logged two straight full practices to begin the week. He remains on track to be a full-go on Sunday in the Super Bowl.

news.head: Drake Maye (shoulder) logs full practice Wednesday
news.body: Drake Maye was a full participant in practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Maye was a full participant as he had told reporters. He remains on track to be a full-go on Sunday.

news.head: Stefon Diggs finds end zone in Week 1 loss to Eagles
news.body: Stefon Diggs hauled in four of his nine targets for 55 yards and one touchdown in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.impact: Diggs saw plenty of volume as part of a Washington passing attack held in check, leading the team in targets in a losing effort. The veteran wideout offers fantasy managers a stable WR2/3 option while the Commanders offense looks to get back on track in a Week 2 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

news.head: Stefon Diggs expected to play against Lions
news.body: Stefon Diggs is set to make his Commanders debut in the preseason on Saturday.
news.impact: Diggs will see his first action as a member of the Commanders. It will be worth tuning in to see what his exact role looks like.

news.head: Stefon Diggs signs with Commanders
news.body: The Washington Commanders have signed WR Stefon Diggs
news.impact: Diggs had been closely linked to Washington for a while. He should step into the immediate No. 2 wide receiver role behind Terry McLaurin. He is coming off a 1,000 yard season with the Patriots. This likely means they won't be signing Brandon Aiyuk.

news.head: Stefon Diggs linked to Commanders
news.body: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Stefon Diggs is "intrigued" by the Commanders.
news.impact: Diggs is drawing interest from at least four other teams. He would step into the immediate WR2 role in Washington alongside Terry McLaurin. He totaled just over 1,000 yards with the Patriots last season coming off a torn ACL. He is now almost two years removed from the injury. He'll likely want to sign with a team soon with training camp starting up.

news.head: Rachaad White sees nine touches in Week 1
news.body: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 22 yards while also catching both of his targets for five yards in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.impact: White made the most of modest touches in the season-opening contest, finishing second to Jacory Croskey-Merritt in touches in the loss. The running back offers more value in PPR formats as the No. 2 backfield option for the Commanders, with a Week 2 contest against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

news.head: Rachaad White (hamstring) off injury report for Sunday
news.body: Rachaad White (hamstring) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.impact: The veteran running back is fully over his hamstring injury at this point and is set to be a full go for Washington's season opener on Sunday. He will be primed for more work if Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is limited or sidelined for the team's matchup against the Eagles.

news.head: Rachaad White (hamstring) set to practice Wednesday
news.body: Rachaad White (hamstring) is set to take part in Washington's practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: White's status for Week 1 is still unclear right now thanks to a hamstring injury that he's still dealing with. He is taking part in Wednesday's practice, however, which is a step in the right direction for him. Fantasy managers should pay attention to updates about his health throughout the week, as Jacory Croskey-Merritt will be a significantly better fantasy option if the veteran is sidelined this week.

news.head: Rachaad White (hamstring) won't play Saturday
news.body: Rachaad White (hamstring) won't play in Saturday's preseason game against the Detroit Lions.
news.impact: White is not going to be available to play in Saturday's preseason game. He is still dealing with a minor hamstring injury, but HC Dan Quinn told reporters that he is "certainly close" to a return to the field. Jacory Croskey-Merritt stands to benefit if this injury causes the veteran to miss more time beyond this game.

news.head: Michael Wilson comes up with five catches in Week 1
news.body: Michael Wilson secured 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.impact: With his next lucrative contract extension in hand, Wilson turned in a decent performance during Sunday's win. The fourth-year receiver finished third on the team in receptions, targets, and receiving yards, maintaining a solid rapport with QB Jacoby Brissett.

news.head: Michael Wilson agrees to three year, $75 million deal with Cardinals
news.body: Michael Wilson has agreed to a three year, $75 million deal with the Arizona Cardinals.
news.impact: Wilson was about to be playing on the final year of his rookie contract, but will now see himself attached to the team for the long haul. It will be interesting to see how his role changes, if at all, under a new coaching stafff and with Marvin Harrison Jr. back in the fold.

news.head: Michael Wilson expected to play role as Z-receiver
news.body: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Michael Wilson will play the Puka Nacua role, “closer to the core,” as the Z-receiver.
news.impact: LaFleur has spent the past three years as the Rams offensive coordinator and figures to bring a lot of what he learned under Sean McVay to the Cardinals offense. Wilson is expected to line up off the line of scrimmage which will allow him to move more freely. Wilson exploded last season when Marvin Harrison Jr. missed time. The question remains what his production will be heading into a full season with Harrison healthy, but he should be put in a more favorable situation.

news.head: Michael Wilson hit pay dirt in Week 18 loss
news.body: Michael Wilson caught 5-of-8 targets for 99 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals 37-20 loss to the Rams.
news.impact: Wilson broke free on a 43-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter. Wilson will end the season on a high note, tallying a touchdown in each of the last five games.

news.head: Jaylen Warren leads Pittsburgh backfield in Week 1
news.body: Jaylen Warren carried the ball 10 times for 46 yards while catching five of his six targets for 27 yards and losing a fumble in a 20-13 win over the Falcons in Week 1.
news.impact: Warren and Rico Dowdle split first-team reps in the preseason, but it was Warren who emerged with the better game in Week 1, out-touching Dowdle 15 to 10 and out-gaining him 73 to 21. Warren will be a flex option for fantasy purposes heading into Week 2 against the Patriots.

news.head: Jaylen Warren, Rico Dowdle both see first-team reps Thursday
news.body: Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle split the first-team reps in practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Warren and Dowdle continue to rotate who sees the first reps with the first-team. They are likely to both be involved in a committee in the Steelers backfield this season.

news.head: Jaylen Warren runs for 66 yards in Week 18
news.body: Jaylen Warren carried the ball 14 times for 66 yards and caught all five of his targets for 33 yards in a 26-24 win over the Ravens in Week 18.
news.impact: Warren was productive in the win, although he was outproduced by Kenneth Gainwell. The two have formed a solid pair in the backfield for Pittsburgh this season. Warren will now prepare to face off against the Texans next week in the Wild-Card round of the playoffs.

news.head: Jaylen Warren logs 12 touches in Week 17 loss
news.body: Jaylen Warren rushed for 64 yards on 12 carries in the Steelers 13-6 loss to the Browns.
news.impact: Warren was not a factor in the passing game, but did see the bulk of the touches in the running game. Unfortunately for fantasy managers, this was far from the wonderful performance he turned in last week. Warren and the Steelers will take on the Ravens in Week 18.

news.head: CeeDee Lamb hauls in touchdown in loss Sunday
news.body: CeeDee Lamb hauled in 5-of-8 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.impact: Lamb was technically Dallas' leading receiver on Sunday night, but he did that with just 44 yards over the course of the game. He was able to haul in a touchdown at one point, however, which helped to salvage his fantasy total on the day. He will likely revert to being an elite producer at the position when Dallas' offense as a whole bounces back sometime within the next few weeks.

news.head: CeeDee Lamb has contract restructured by Cowboys
news.body: The Cowboys restructured the contract of WR CeeDee Lamb.
news.impact: Lamb was one of three players who had their contracts restructured to help create a significant amount of capital space for the Cowboys. They are now under the cap heading into free agency. Lamb and George Pickens are expected to run it back with Dak Prescott in the passing game for Dallas.

news.head: CeeDee Lamb catches just one pass in Week 18
news.body: CeeDee Lamb caught his only target for four yards in Sunday's loss to the Giants.
news.impact: The Cowboys limited most of their starters' snaps in Week 18, and Lamb was no exception. The four-time Pro-Bowler made his 75th catch of the season Sunday, as he finished the campaign with 1,077 yards and three touchdowns over 14 games.

news.head: CeeDee Lamb sees 10 targets in Week 17 win over Commanders
news.body: CeeDee Lamb hauled in five of his team-high 10 targets for 46 yards in the Cowboys' 30-23 Week 17 win over the Commanders.
news.impact: Lamb continues a productive stretch in the Dallas passing attack, recording 75 or more receiving yards in four of his last six games. The dynamic wideout remains a reliable WR1 option for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 18 matchup against the New York Giants.

news.head: Jacksonville Jaguars D/ST shut down hapless Browns
news.body: The Jacksonville Jaguars D/ST shut down the Browns' offense on Sunday in the team's dominant 34-10 win. They ended the day with five sacks, a pick, and a fumble recovery.
news.impact: It was a great day for the Jags' defense in what was expected to be an easy matchup. They're worth streaming when the matchup is right, but they could be in for tough sledding against Denver next week.

news.head: Jacksonville Jaguars D/ST shut down Titans in dominant win
news.body: The Jacksonville Jaguars D/ST got a sack and a pick-six in the Jaguars' 41-7 win over the Titans.
news.impact: The Jaguars didn't have multiple takeaways or many sacks, but they simply sucked the life out of the Titans' offense. That's not to say they didn't make great plays; they certainly did, and they counted for fantasy big time. They are coming into the playoffs on a hot streak.

news.head: Jaguars D/ST records two interceptions Sunday
news.body: The Jaguars D/ST allowed 17 points on 204 yards with two interceptions and two sacks on Sunday against the Colts.
news.impact: The second interception on the day came on a Hail Mary thrown by Riley Leonard on the final play of the game. They should be worth starting again in Week 18 against the Titans.

news.head: Jaguars D/ST allows 20 points Sunday
news.body: The Jaguars' D/ST logged one sack, one interception, and one fumble recovery while allowing 20 points in Sunday's win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Jacksonville's defense had a pretty good game against the Broncos on Sunday. They allowed just 20 points and were able to log a couple of key takeaways to help secure the win on the road. This unit had a good schedule to close out the season, with matchups against the Colts and Titans coming up over the next couple of weeks.

news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt reaches end zone in Week 1 loss
news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt carried the ball 16 times for 63 yards and one touchdown while also catching his only target for a loss of seven yards in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt made the most of his opportunities out of the backfield, accounting for 50% of the carries for the Commanders in Week 1. The running back seems poised to receive as much volume as he can handle as the primary option out of the backfield to begin the season for head coach Dan Quinn, with a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) will play in Week 1
news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) will play in Week 1 for the Washington Commanders against the Philadelphia Eagles according to Ian Rapoport.

news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) limited participant Wednesday
news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt is managing a groin injury right now and was unable to log a full practice session on Wednesday as a result. There's an off-chance that it will leave him sidelined for Week 1, which would lead to more work for Rachaad White against the Eagles.

news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) returns to practice
news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt returned to practice on Tuesday.
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt was absent from practice for the past week. He should be on track to be good to go for Week 1.

news.head: De'Von Achane sees 15 touches in Week 1 loss to Raiders
news.body: De'Von Achane carried the ball 11 times for 36 yards while also hauling in four of his five targets for 30 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 Week 1 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.impact: Achane was unable to find much running room out of the backfield in the season opener, with the Las Vegas defense challenging new starting quarterback Malik Willis to beat it through the air. The running back remains a dynamic option in PPR formats, but fantasy managers may need to temper expectations in the short term, with a Week 2 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.head: De'Von Achane (shoulder) cleared to practice
news.body: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said De'Von Achane is ready to go after offseason shoulder surgery.
news.impact: Achane didn't participate in team drills this spring as he rehabbed, but he's good to go now that training camp's here. He'll be in line for his workhorse role as the focal point of the Dolphins offense.

news.head: De'Von Achane (shoulder) sees uptick in reps in minicamp Tuesday
news.body: Dolphins RB De'Von Achane reportedly saw an uptick in practice activity at Tuesday’s minicamp session.
news.impact: Achane is continuing to work his way back from an offseason procedure on his shoulder. He is expected to be good to go for training camp.

news.head: De'Von Achane (shoulder) hopeful to be ready for training camp
news.body: De'Von Achane told reporters he hopes to return to full action by training camp.
news.impact: Achane, who is fresh off a contract extension, underwent a clean-up procedure on his shoulder during the offseason. He hasn't been fully cleared yet, but he is hopeful to be good to go by training camp. He has still been practicing in limited fashion.

news.head: George Pickens held to 28 yards Sunday
news.body: George Pickens caught 3-of-6 targets for just 28 yards in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.impact: Pickens had an extremely disappointing start to the season on Sunday night. He was held to just 28 yards on three catches in the team's first game of the season after being hyped up as an elite fantasy prospect throughout the preseason. He should bounce back and play better than this moving forward, but his week-to-week floor may be lower than some realize if Dallas' offense struggles with consistency this season.

news.head: George Pickens to play 2026 season on franchise tag with Cowboys
news.body: George Pickens will officially play the 2026 season on a $27.3 million franchise tag for the Dallas Cowboys.
news.impact: Pickens and the Cowboys could not agree upon a long-term extension this summer, so he will head into the year effectively on a 1-year deal. The wideout is coming off a career year in which he hauled in 93 catches for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns. He will head into this season with Dallas firmly in the WR1 conversation in fantasy.

news.head: George Pickens expected to move around formation more this season
news.body: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said he plans to move WR George Pickens around the formation more this season.
news.impact: Pickens has reported to mandatory minicamp after sitting out of voluntary OTAs. He is expected to play both on the outside and in the slot, adding to the versatility he will offer the Cowboys offense.

news.head: George Pickens goes through individual drills in practice Wednesday
news.body: George Pickens went through individual drills on Day 2 of Cowboys minicamp on Wednesday.
news.impact: Pickens reported on Tuesday for the start of mandatory minicamp. He is expected to be a full-go in practice by training camp.

news.head: Tyler Allgeier leads Arizona rushing attack in Week 1
news.body: Tyler Allgeier gained 61 yards on 17 carries and nine yards on two receptions in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.impact: Allgeier shouldered the majority of the backfield load for the Cardinals on Sunday, getting six more carries than Jeremiyah Love. Allgeier was not especially impressive, averaging just 3.6 yards per carry with a long of 11. Allgeier will remain involved, but the share of the carries should tilt more toward Love as the rookie gets further removed from the ankle sprain he sustained a month ago.

news.head: Tyler Allgeier listed as starter on Cardinals depth chart
news.body: Tyler Allgeier was listed as the starting running back on the Cardinals' Week 1 depth chart.
news.impact: Allgeier was listed as the starter ahead of rookie Jeremiyah Love after a training camp battle. Love has also been making his way back from an ankle sprain, which could be why Allgeier sees more carries in the early part of the season. If he does indeed get the start on Sunday, Allgeier could be an RB3 or deeper flex option in fantasy.

news.head: Tyler Allgeier signs two-year deal with Cardinals
news.body: The Cardinals agreed to terms on a two-year, $12.25 million deal with Tyler Allgeier.
news.impact: Allgeier joins James Conner and Trey Benson in the backfield for Arizona. He had potential other landing spots where he could have had more of a feature role if Conner remains in Arizona. This will remain a backfield to monitor the rest of the offseason.

news.head: Tyler Allgeier linked to Seahawks
news.body: The Seahawks are expected to have interest in free agent RB Tyler Allgeier.
news.impact: Allgeier is set to enter free agency next week. He should draw some interest from several teams. The Seahawks are expected to have interest as they're expected to be out of the market to re-sign Kenneth Walker.

news.head: Jordan Addison fails to catch pass Sunday
news.body: Jordan Addison did not catch either of his two targets in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.impact: Justin Jefferson dominated the targets after Carson Wentz took over behind center. Addison will be in the WR3/WR4 mix heading into Week 2 against a vulnerable Bears defense.

news.head: Jordan Addison (thumb) to miss day or two of practice
news.body: Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said WR Jordan Addison will miss a day or two after jamming his thumb.
news.impact: Addison underwent tests that showed the injury will be short-term. He could return to practice by this weekend.

news.head: Jordan Addison officially has fifth-year option picked up by Vikings
news.body: The Vikings have officially exercised Jordan Addison's fifth-year option.
news.impact: It was reported over a month ago and it is now official. Addison has shown flashes of his potential across his first three seasons, while also being suspended three games for violating the league’s substance abuse policy. He was also arrested for misdemeanor trespassing charges earlier this offseason.

news.head: Jordan Addison gets fifth-year option picked up
news.body: The Minnesota Vikings have exercised the fifth-year option on WR Jordan Addison.
news.impact: Addison’s contract is now guaranteed through 2027. He projects as a mid-to-low-end WR3 heading into fantasy draft season.

news.head: Jordan Mason being evaluated for sore thumb
news.body: Vikings head coach O'Connell said RB Jordan Mason is being evaluated for a sore thumb.
news.impact: Mason came into the building on Monday with the injury. He is day-to-day for now after leading the backfield on Sunday.

news.head: Jordan Mason sees 15 carries Sunday
news.body: Jordan Mason ran for 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.impact: Mason led the way in the Vikings backfield as both he and Aaron Jones saw double-digit carries. He will be in the low-end RB2 conversation next week against the Bears.

news.head: Jordan Mason rushes for game-high 94 yards Sunday
news.body: Jordan Mason carried the ball 14 times for 94 yards as the Vikings defeated the Packers, 16-3, in the regular season finale.
news.impact: Mason finished his first season in Minnesota as the team's leading rusher with 758 yards despite only starting five games for the Vikings. His 94 yards on the ground on Sunday was his second-highest total of the season. With both Mason and Aaron Jones on affordable contracts for next season, the duo figure to form a similar backfield timeshare in 2026.

news.head: Jordan Mason (ankle) removed from injury report for Week 18
news.body: Jordan Mason has been removed from the injury report for Sunday's game against the Packers.
news.impact: Aaron Jones was ruled out. Mason should lead the backfield in the season finale as a result.

news.head: Keaton Mitchell gets sparse action in Week 1
news.body: Keaton Mitchell gained nine yards on four carries in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.impact: After Sunday's season opener, Mitchell is clearly little more than a handcuff for Chargers lead back Omarion Hamption. Still, it is worth noting that Mitchell had been dealing with a hamstring issue as recently as last week. The fourth-year back has shown plenty of big-play ability over the last three seasons in Baltimore, but it would likely require an injury to Hampton for Mitchell to offer much fantasy value.

news.head: Keaton Mitchell (hamstring) off injury report for Sunday
news.body: Keaton Mitchell (hamstring) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.
news.impact: Mitchell has been dealing with a nagging hamstring injury for a while, but it appears he is finally over it, as he has received full clearance to suit up and play for the Chargers in their season opener. He will remain relegated to a depth role behind Omarion Hampton for the foreseeable future, however.

news.head: Keaton Mitchell (hamstring) limited participant Wednesday
news.body: Keaton Mitchell (hamstring) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Mitchell was sidelined for a while as he dealt with a hamstring injury, but he was able to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday. He will have a chance to play in Week 1, but even if he's active, he's not expected to play more than a depth role for the Chargers in their matchup against the Cardinals.

news.head: Keaton Mitchell returns to practice Monday
news.body: Keaton Mitchell was back at Chargers practice on Monday.
news.impact: Mitchell had missed the last six practices. His return on Monday is a good sign for his status heading into Sunday's season opener.

news.head: Javonte Williams scores twice in loss Sunday
news.body: Javonte Williams rushed the ball 12 times for 41 yards and a touchdown and caught five passes for 31 yards and another touchdown in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.impact: Williams was arguably Dallas' most impactful offensive player on Sunday night. He scored two touchdowns and totaled 72 yards on a night where the entire offense struggled, leaving him with a surprisingly good fantasy total on the week. He is clearly the team's bellcow running back at this point and should be viewed as a high quality fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

news.head: Javonte Williams remains Cowboys lead back in 2026
news.body: Javonte Williams remains as Dallas’ lead back by a comfortable margin headed into 2026 following a breakout campaign that ended with him signing a three year extension with the team.
news.impact: Williams has the bell-cow, or at least the lead role, on lockdown. However, what’s primarily in question is who will be backing him up, as Jaydon Blue, Malik Davis, and Phil Mafah are all vying for the role. It appears Dallas, while comfortable with Williams, doesn’t want to put the same sort of workload on him again this season as he had in 2025. That could hurt his upside unless he becomes more proficient in the passing game, but on volume alone he should maintain RB2 status.

news.head: Javonte Williams lands three year deal with Dallas
news.body: Javonte Williams has landed a three year deal with the Dallas Cowboys, with $16 million guaranteed.
news.impact: The former Bronco cashes in after a big season in Dallas. Expectations were fairly low for the veteran back, who was coming off of multiple injuries and disappointing seasons, but he crushed expectations to the tune of 1,200 rushing yards and 11 rushing touchdowns. He is a strong RB2 heading into 2026 with RB1 upside.

news.head: Javonte Williams (shoulder/neck) placed on IR
news.body: Javonte Williams (shoulder/neck) has been placed on Injured Reserve with shoulder and neck injuries.
news.impact: Williams was ruled out for Week 18, with Jaydon Blue expected to take on the workload in his absence. It’s a sad end to an otherwise great season for Williams, who will likely see a lot of interest from teams in free agency, but don’t be surprised if he comes back to Dallas.

news.head: Brenton Strange grabs touchdown in win over Browns
news.body: Brenton Strange caught two of three targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday.
news.impact: Strange was among ten other targeted receivers who were trying to feast off of an extremely small pie of 21 total targets. And he was one of the lucky ones with a touchdown. He should continue to see work as the top tight end for the offense, but things are so spread out that it might be hard to rely on him on a weekly basis.

news.head: Brenton Strange signs three-year extension with Jaguars
news.body: The Jaguars signed Brenton Strange to a three-year contract extension.
news.impact: The deal is worth “up to” $48 million with $25 million guaranteed. Strange missed five games last season, but emerged as a top threat in the passing game when he was healthy for Trevor Lawrence last season. Strange profiles as a borderline TE1 for fantasy managers with Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol competing for snaps behind him.

news.head: Brenton Strange could be offense’s most important player’ behind Lawrence
news.body: Brenton Strange could the the Jags ‘“most important player” aside from Trevor Lawrence, according to Jags beat John Shipley. Shipley notes than despite missing five games last year, Strange still finished third in routes run.
news.impact: Strange is far and away the Jags TE1, and it doesn’t seem anyone is taking that job away from him. Tanner Koziol is next up as a pass catcher, but the rookie out of Houston is the TE3 at the moment and unlikely to impact Strange’s workload.

news.head: Brenton Strange snags touchdown in win
news.body: Brenton Strange caught all six of his targets for 52 yards and a score in the Jaguars' 41-7 win over the Titans.
news.impact: Strange closed out the season with some nice numbers and was a viable tight end streamer. He had at least five targets in five of the Jaguars' last seven games, with three touchdowns to boot. It will be tough for him to be a high-end fantasy tight end given his target competition, but he should be a decent streamer in the right matchup in 2026.

news.head: Chargers D/ST doesn't accomplish much in Week 1 loss
news.body: The Chargers allowed 26 points on 393 yards of total offense in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.impact: The Chargers did not force a turnover and came up with just one sack in Sunday's season-opening letdown. The L.A. defense did at least provide some friction in the red zone, limiting the Cardinals to two touchdowns in five trips, but this was still a mediocre effort overall. Arizona QB Jacoby Brissett largely picked the Chargers apart with accurate passing from a clean pocket while the Cardinals' running game churned out 116 yards and a touchdown. The Chargers will look to shore things up for a Week 2 matchup with the Raiders.

news.head: Mike McDaniel expected to be named Chargers OC
news.body: The Chargers are expected to name Mike McDaniel their next offensive coordinator.
news.impact: McDaniel had drawn interest from other teams in both a head coach and offensive coordinator role. It was announced earlier on Tuesday that he had taken his name out of the race to be the Cleveland Browns next head coach. He will likely bring a faster-paced offense to the Chargers led by Justin Herbert through the air and Omarion Hampton on the ground. This should lead to more upside for the Chargers offense as a whole heading into next season.

news.head: Chargers D/ST logs four sacks Sunday
news.body: The Chargers' D/ST logged four sacks and allowed 13 points in Sunday's loss to the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Los Angeles' defense had a sneaky good game on Sunday, allowing Denver's starters to score just 13 points over the course of the game. This unit is on something of a hot streak, as they have only allowed their opponent to score more than 20 points just once in the last ten weeks. They could give the Patriots a run for their money in the Wild Card round if they can keep that momentum up.

news.head: Los Angeles Chargers D/ST picks off Houston twice in loss
news.body: The Los Angeles Chargers D/ST picked off Houston QB CJ Stroud twice but failed to register a sack in the Chargers' 20-16 loss to the Texans.
news.impact: The Chargers' defense was fine against the Texans, but a sack or two would have been nice for fantasy managers. They've been a great unit for much of the last month, but will face a tough test against Denver next Sunday.

news.head: Kayshon Boutte makes only catch in Texans debut
news.body: Kayshon Boutte caught 1-of-2 targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Boutte was acquired from New England late in the preseason to shore up the Texans' wide receiver corps. His big-play potential is known from the last couple of years with the Patriots, but his targets were predictably limited in an offense that is still relatively new to him. Boutte is a wait-and-see bench stash in standard fantasy leagues.

news.head: Kayshon Boutte will play in Week 1
news.body: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Kayshon Boutte will play in Week 1 against the Bills.
news.impact: Boutte was acquired in a trade with the Patriots back on August 24. Ryans said he has been “picking up the playbook really well.” He'll be a deep threat on the outside for CJ Stroud.

news.head: Kayshon Boutte traded to Texans
news.body: The Patriots are sending WR Kayshon Boutte to the Texans in exchange for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round pick.
news.impact: Boutte has had his name in trade rumors for most of the offseason following the Patriots offseason additions of AJ Brown and Romeo Doubs. Boutte will get a fresh start in a wide open wide receiver room with Houston. He should compete for a role as a field stretcher for the Texans.

news.head: Kayshon Boutte significantly involved in Tuesday's practice
news.body: Kayshon Boutte was significantly involved in Tuesday's practice.
news.impact: Boutte reported to minicamp despite his name being in the middle of trade rumors. It will continue to be something to monitor heading into training camp.

news.head: Travis Hunter quiet in win over Browns
news.body: Travis Hunter had one catch for eight yards and one carry for three yards in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday. On defense, he had one solo tackle.
news.impact: No matter if you play in offense only or in IDP leagues, Hunter is not a player you're happy with right now. His production and usage isn't that of a first-round NFL pick, especially at second overall. The Jaguars are content to use him as a gadget player, and until that changes, he needs to be off of fantasy radars unless you are in dynasty formats.

news.head: Travis Hunter (knee) practices Wednesday
news.body: Travis Hunter was back on the practice field in training camp on Wednesday.
news.impact: Hunter is back on the field from last year’s knee injury. He continues to see reps on both sides of the ball in practice.

news.head: Travis Hunter unsure when he will be full-go in practice
news.body: The Jaguars are unsure when Travis Hunter will be a full-go in practice.
news.impact: Hunter tore his LCL late in October 2025 and missed the rest of his rookie season, which he is still working his way back from. He is expected to play on both sides of the ball this season with more of an emphasis on the defensive side of the ball.

news.head: Travis Hunter expected to enter camp as 'full-time CB, part-time WR'
news.body: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that the expectation is Travis Hunter will enter training camp as a "full-time corner back and part-time wide receiver."
news.impact: This was seeming inevitable to end last season with the emergence of Parker Washington and acquisition of Jakobi Meyers. It is a brutal blow for dynasty managers who drafted Hunter early last season. He will remain a player to continue to monitor for fantasy managers.

news.head: Jayden Reed quiet Sunday
news.body: Jayden Reed caught 3-of-7 targets for 20 yards in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings.
news.impact: The seven targets were encouraging, but Reed was not anywhere near as productive as Christian Watson and Matthew Golden to open the season. He is a WR4/WR5 heading into Week 2.

news.head: Jayden Reed (ankle) returns to practice Tuesday
news.body: Jayden Reed was back at practice on Tuesday.
news.impact: Reed makes his way back after being sidelined for a few days. He worked his way back from an ankle injury.

news.head: Jayden Reed (ankle) not expected to practice Monday
news.body: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said he does not expect WR Jayden Reed to practice on Monday.
news.impact: Reed also missed practice on Sunday. He remains day-to-day. It is unknown how serious his injury is.

news.head: Jayden Reed (ankle) not practicing Sunday
news.body: Jayden Reed did not practice on Sunday due to an ankle injury.
news.impact: It is unclear how serious the injury is for Reed, who signed a three-year extension with Green Bay this offseason. He is day-to-day going into the week. There should be an update provided by coach Matt LaFleur when available.

news.head: Sam LaPorta catches five passes in Week 1 win
news.body: Sam LaPorta caught five of his eight targets for 48 yards in the Lions' 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.impact: LaPorta saw sizeable volume in his return to the lineup for head coach Dan Campbell, joining explosive wideouts Jameson Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown in finishing with eight or more targets in the win. The tight end remains a stable option in all formats as a primary pass-catching option in the Detroit offense ahead of a Week 2 contest against the Buffalo Bills.

news.head: Sam LaPorta (hip) off injury report for Sunday
news.body: Sam LaPorta (hip) is off of the injury report ahead of Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.
news.impact: LaPorta is now off of the injury report after dealing with a hip injury for the latter part of the preseason. He should be a full go for Week 1 and will remain a startable fantasy option in this matchup and beyond.

news.head: Sam LaPorta (hip) returns to practice Tuesday
news.body: Sam Laporta returned to practice on Tuesday after suffering a hip injury last week.
news.impact: Laporta's hip injury has made his status for Week 1 murky, but his returning to practice this early is a good sign. The tight end will likely be limited as he builds back up, but he could be in line to start the season barring any setbacks.

news.head: Sam LaPorta suffers hip injury, uncertain for Week 1
news.body: Sam LaPorta is currently dealing with a hip injury, and HC Dan Campbell told reporters that the team is uncertain if it will affect his availability for Week 1.
news.impact: LaPorta injured his hip on a hit in practice recently. The team is uncertain about the severity of it at this point and will be giving him a few days off to rest and recover before reevaluating. Fantasy managers should pay close attention to this situation, as he may not be worth drafting at his current ADP if he has to miss one or more games at the start of the regular season.

news.head: Kaelon Black impresses in win over Rams
news.body: Kaelon Black ran 14 times for 65 yards and caught his only target for five yards in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams on Thursday.
news.impact: Black was in a full-on committee with Christian McCaffrey, something few, if any, saw coming. Both were tied at 15 touches apiece, but McCaffrey led in total opportunities thanks to seeing more targets. Black won't have games like this all the time, but he's showing himself to be a valuable handcuff that CMC managers will need to snag when they can.

news.head: Kaelon Black (adductor) in uniform at practice Tuesday
news.body: Kaelon Black is in uniform at practice on Tuesday for the first time since the first week of camp.
news.impact: It is a positive sign for the Black. The rookie will have a chance to be good to go for the regular season opener.

news.head: Kaelon Black (adductor) not practicing Monday
news.body: Kaelon Black missed practice on Monday with an adductor injury.
news.impact: With Jordan James sidelined with a fractured rib, Black was seeing more opportunity to compete for the RB2 role in the 49ers backfield. He is day-to-day for now.

news.head: Kaelon Black selected No. 90 by San Francisco 49ers
news.body: The San Francisco 49ers have selected RB Kaelon Black with the No. 90 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.impact: Black becomes the latest running back addition in the draft by the 49ers. He showcased his upside in the run by Indiana to winning the national championship this past year. He is a shorter running back who is strong with good vision. He will compete for a depth role in the 49ers backfield.

news.head: Derrick Henry rushes for three touchdowns in Week 1 win over Colts
news.body: Derrick Henry carried the ball 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns while also hauling in his lone target for 19 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.impact: Henry capitalized on a sizeable workload out of the Baltimore backfield, averaging an impressive 6.0 yards per carry in the Week 1 win. The superstar running back remains locked in as a reliable RB1 ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

news.head: Derrick Henry rushes for 126 yards in Week 18
news.body: Derrick Henry carried the ball 20 times for 126 yards in a 26-24 loss to the Steelers in Week 18.
news.impact: Henry was unable to corral his lone target in the contest. With the loss, the Ravens will miss the playoffs in a disappointing ending to the season. Henry finishes the year with 1,595 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns while appearing in all 17 games. He will remain a solid RB1 for fantasy purposes heading into the 2026 season.

news.head: Derrick Henry has historic night against Packers
news.body: Derrick Henry ran 36 times for 216 yards and four touchdowns in the Ravens' 41-24 win over the Packers on Saturday.
news.impact: Henry's performance could easily be what decides the title for many fantasy championships. His 36 rush attempts were a career high in a single game, and his four touchdowns tied his career high in touchdowns in a game. Henry now has over 1,400 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns this season, a great total. The King is still on the throne.

news.head: Derrick Henry scores two touchdowns in loss Sunday
news.body: Derrick Henry rushed the ball 18 times for 128 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday night's 28-24 loss to the New England Patriots.
news.impact: Henry was dominant for most of Sunday night's game, totaling 128 yards and two touchdowns on the ground while maintaining great efficiency at 7.1 yards per carry. He coughed up a costly fumble in the second half and didn't really take the field again after that, however. He will likely continue to be a decent fantasy option over the last couple weeks of the season, though his upside will be limited if Lamar Jackson (back) is sidelined for the Ravens.

news.head: Drake London held to two catches in Week 1 loss
news.body: Drake London caught two of his four targets for 29 yards in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1. He also gained six yards on his lone carry in the game.
news.impact: London was quiet in the close loss, although his 29 receiving yards were good enough for him to finish second on the Falcons in that category. The Falcons were forced to play Cooper Rush, their third-string QB, thanks to injuries, so London should bounce back once either Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix is ready to return to the field. London sets up as a low-end WR1 heading into Week 2 against Carolina.

news.head: Drake London: Extension is 'on top of mind' per GM Ian Cunningham
news.body: Falcons GM Ian Cunningham said an extension for Drake London is “on top of mind.”
news.impact: It appears an extension could be agreed to after the NFL Draft. London is entering the final year of his rookie contract. There should be a new deal agreed to at some point later in the offseason.

news.head: Drake London finds the end zone in Week 18
news.body: Drake London caught 4-of-8 targets for 78 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons 19-17 win over the Saints.
news.impact: Despite struggling with Kirk Cousins to end the season, London closed the year on a high note with a touchdown. He missed the 1,000 yard mark after missing five games. He is set to head into the final year of his rookie deal where he should remain a WR1 for fantasy managers.

news.head: Drake London (knee) officially active for Week 18
news.body: Falcons WR Drake London (knee) is officially active for Week 18.
news.impact: London was listed as questionable after being limited in practice this week. He will remain the top pass catcher for Kirk Cousins and the Falcons against the Saints.

news.head: Luther Burden III sees six touches in Week 1
news.body: Luther Burden III hauled in all five of his targets for 63 yards while also rushing once for two yards in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Burden III saw steady involvement in the Chicago passing attack, finishing second on the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the win. The wideout offers head coach Ben Johnson another dynamic pass-catcher as part of an explosive Chicago offense ahead of a Week 2 divisional matchup with the Minnesota Vikings.

news.head: Luther Burden III (groin) good to go for Week 1
news.body: Luther Burden III (groin) is off of the injury report and good to go for Week 1's matchup against the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Burden was dealing with a groin injury earlier in the offseason, but he is fully healthy now and carries no injury designation ahead of Sunday's season opener. He should play without any restrictions and will be primed for a huge Week 1 if the Bears are without Rome Odunze (calf) for their matchup against the Panthers.

news.head: Luther Burden III (groin) practices Tuesday
news.body: Luther Burden III was practicing on Tuesday.
news.impact: Burden had returned to practice last week. He is on track to be good to go for the start of the season next week.

news.head: Luther Burden III (groin) back at practice Wednesday
news.body: Luther Burden III returned to practicing on Wednesday.
news.impact: Burden was back on the field for the first time since injuring his groin on August 8. He went through individual drills and went inside when 7 on 7 started. This should put him on track to be good to go for Week 1.

news.head: Khalil Shakir goes for 50 yards in win
news.body: Khalil Shakir caught four of six targets for 50 yards in the Bills’ 36-31 win over Houston on Sunday.
news.impact: Shakir operated as Josh Allen’s safety valve underneath with DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid working over the top. That’s been Shakir’s role in the past, so don’t expect it to stop any time soon. His upside is capped because of it, but he’s a decent flex play in PPR formats if you need a solid floor.

news.head: Khalil Shakir good to go for Sunday
news.body: Khalil Shakir will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Houston Texans.
news.impact: Shakir was a full participant at practice on Wednesday and is expected to be fully good to go for Sunday's season opener against the Houston Texans. He is not worth starting for fantasy purposes at this point, however, especially with DJ Moore now in town for the Bills.

news.head: Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) seen practicing Wednesday
news.body: Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) was seen practicing for the Bills on Wednesday.
news.impact: Shakir's availability for Week 1 is currently up in the air due to an undisclosed injury that he's dealing with. He was spotted at practice on Wednesday, however, which bodes well for his availability for the season opener. It remains unclear if he was a limited or full participant.

news.head: Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) 'optimistic' for Week 1
news.body: There's "currently optimism” from the Bills that Khalil Shakir will play in Week 1 against the Texans.
news.impact: Shakir has been sidelined from practice for the past couple of weeks due to an undisclosed injury. Buffalo is reportedly being cautious with him.

news.head: Harrison Mevis kicks single PAT in loss to Niners
news.body: Harrison Mevis made his only PAT attempt in the Rams' 27-7 tough loss to the 49ers.
news.impact: Mevis wasn't called upon much, the Rams offense was just never in scoring position for most of the game. He could have come in in the second half, but the Rams elected to go for it on 4th and goal at the 1 yard line, which was the correct choice, but their failure to convert meant Mevis was going to have an even bigger stinker. Brighter days are ahead for the Rams kicker.

news.head: Harrison Mevis returns to Rams after being tendered Monday
news.body: Harrison Mevis has been tendered by the Rams and will return to Los Angeles for the 2026 season.
news.impact: Undrafted out of Missouri in 2024, Mevis was a revelation for both the Rams and for fantasy owners last season. He replaced Joshua Karty as Los Angeles' kicker midway through they year and went 12-for-13 on field goal tries and a perfect 39-of-39 on extra point attempts in nine regular season games. He was also perfect in three postseason contests, going 6-for-6 on field goals and 9-for-9 on PATs. Mevis will open 2026 as the Rams' primary kicker and, given the potency of Los Angeles' offense, should be in line for a big year.

news.head: Harrison Mevis perfect in Week 18
news.body: Harrison Mevis connected on 3-of-3 field goals and 4-of-4 extra points in the Rams 37-20 win over the Cardinals.
news.impact: Mevis connected on field goals from 34, 40, and 42 yards out in the win. Mevis will end his first season with the Rams 12-of-13 on field goal attempts and 39-of-39 on extra point attempts.

news.head: Harrison Mevis goes for 5 points on Monday night
news.body: Harrison Mevis hit all three of his PATs and his only field goal in the Rams’ 27-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday night.
news.impact: Mevis didn’t have the greatest day for fantasy, the offense was shut out in the first half and struggled to do much until the final quarter. He’s been a solid kicker for the Rams this season and should be a fine fantasy asset if he returns in 2026.

news.head: A.J. Brown (ankle) out at least six weeks
news.body: A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss at least six weeks for the New England Patriots according to Ian Rapoport.
news.impact: Brown was placed on injured reserve after suffering the ankle injury in New England’s Week 1 loss to the Seattle Seahawks Wednesday night, leaving head coach Mike Vrable without his top pass-catching option for the foreseeable future. In the wideout’s absence Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs, and DeMario Douglas will need to step up for quarterback Drake Maye early in the season.

news.head: A.J. Brown (ankle) placed on injured reserve
news.body: A.J. Brown (ankle) has been placed on injured reserve by the New England Patriots according to Adam Schefter.

news.head: A.J. Brown (ankle) expect to miss at least four weeks
news.body: A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss at least four weeks with a high ankle sprain that he sustained early in the third quarter of the Patriots game against the Seahawks on Wednesday night.
news.impact: It’s a big blow to Brown’s Fantasy stock to start the season. In his absence, expect Hunter Henry and Romeo Doubs to see more work. However, with Doubs was struggling to find snaps and catch the ball, it’s possible that Demario Douglas could be a nice PPR sleeper.

news.head: A.J. Brown (ankle) believed to have suffered high-ankle sprain on Wednesday
news.body: A.J. Brown (ankle) is believed to have suffered a high ankle sprain in last nights game against the Seahawks. He will have an MRI today to determine the extent of the injury and how much time he will miss.
news.impact: It’s a tough start to Browns Patriot tenure. He went down early in the third quarter and did not return, leaving Drake Maye to lean on Hunter Henry, Demario Douglas, and Mack Hollins with fellow newcomer Romeo Doubs struggling to catch anything. Doubs should bounce back, and if Brown is out for any period of time, expect Doubs and Henry to have some more fantasy appeal, with Douglas as a PPR dart throw in deep formats.

news.head: Rashee Rice finds end zone in win Monday
news.body: Rashee Rice caught two passes for 19 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Rice had an underwhelming game on Monday night. He was held to just two catches for 19 yards against the Broncos, but he was able to get into the end zone on one of those receptions, which helped to salvage his fantasy total. QB Patrick Mahomes II didn't look his way very much in this game, but it seems like the team wanted Mahomes to drop back as little as possible given that it was his first game back from a major knee injury. Rice will likely improve going forward, but fantasy managers should keep a close eye on his production over the next few weeks to gauge whether this poor showing was a fluke or a sign of the things to come for the veteran wideout this season.

news.head: Rashee Rice (knee) active for Week 1
news.body: Rashee Rice (knee) is active for Week 1 for the Kansas City Chiefs against the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Rice will suit up after progressing throughout the practice week and not suffering any issues in pregame activities, providing quarterback Patrick Mahomes with all of his pass-catching weapons against the Broncos Monday night.

news.head: Rashee Rice (knee) logs full practice Thursday
news.body: Rashee Rice (knee) logged a full practice session on Thursday.
news.impact: As expected, Rice was able to log a full practice session on Thursday and seems to be set to play in Monday night's game against the Denver Broncos. Despite the tough matchup, he projects to be a good fantasy option in PPR leagues this week, especially with Patrick Mahomes II (knee) likely to be at the helm for Kansas City.

news.head: Rashee Rice (knee) takes part in 11-on-11 drills Wednesday
news.body: Rashee Rice was able to progress to taking part in 11-on-11 drills at practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Rice has been recovering from arthroscopic surgery on his right knee in May. He was able to participate in 11-on-11 drills for the first time in camp as he continues to progress in the right direction.

news.head: Ka'imi Fairbairn puts seven points on the board
news.body: Ka'imi Fairbairn made his only field-goal try and all four of his PATs in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Fairbairn showed off his powerful leg in Sunday's loss, nailing a 58-yard attempt to briefly give the Texans a one-point lead in the fourth quarter. The veteran has been kicking for the Texans since 2017 and remains one of the more reliable options in the league.

news.head: Ka'imi Fairbairn re-signs with Texans
news.body: The Texans re-signed K Ka'imi Fairbairn to a two-year, $13 million deal.
news.impact: Fairbairn will remain in Houston for two more years. He remains one of the top kickers in the NFL and for fantasy managers.

news.head: Ka'imi Fairbairn connects on six field goals in Week 18
news.body: Ka'imi Fairbairn connected on 6-of-6 field goals in Week 18 against the Colts.
news.impact: Fairbairn finishes the season connecting on 44-of-48 field goals. He should continue to be needed heading into the playoffs.

news.head: Ka'imi Fairbairn puts up 8 kicking points in win
news.body: Ka'imi Fairbairn made both of his PATs and both of his field goal attempts in the Texans' 20-16 win over the Chargers on Saturday.
news.impact: Fairbairn had a nice game despite the low overall scoring. The Texans' offense is humming this year, and Fairbairn has had fewer than seven kicking points just once all season.

news.head: Isiah Pacheco (back/knee) out for 12 weeks after undergoing back surgery
news.body: Isiah Pacheco (back/knee) is out for at least the next 12 weeks after undergoing surgery to remove a body that was pressing a nerve on his neck. The plan is to have him back in early December.
news.impact: It’s a tough blow to Pacheco, who was already struggling with a knee injury. He’s droppable in all formats, as his handcuff status for 2026 is pretty much out the window.

news.head: Isiah Pacheco (back/MCL) placed in injured reserve
news.body: Isiah Pacheco (back/MCL) has been placed on injured reserve by the Detroit Lions Tuesday according to Ari Meirov.
news.impact: Pacheco will be sidelined for at least the first four games of the upcoming regular season, with his first opportunity to return coming ahead of a Week 5 contest against the Arizona Cardinals. Jacob Saylors will slide into the No. 2 running back role behind superstar Jahmyr Gibbs in the Lions backfield after an impressive preseason for the time being, with the Lions likely to add more depth to a shorthanded running backs room prior to the regular season.

news.head: Isiah Pacheco dealing with back injury in addition to MCL sprain
news.body: Lions coach Dan Campbell said Isiah Pacheco is dealing with a back injury in addition to his MCL sprain.
news.impact: Pacheco remains without a clear timetable to return. The Lions recently worked out Kareem Hunt.

news.head: Isiah Pacheco dealing with sprained MCL, should be good to go Week 1
news.body: Lions coach Dan Campbell said Isiah Pacheco is dealing with a sprained MCL but should be good to go in time for Week 1.
news.impact: “We feel pretty good about him being ready to go, especially when the season gets here," Campbell said. Pacheco is slated to open the season backing up Jahmyr Gibbs.

news.head: David Montgomery has big debut for Texans
news.body: David Montgomery rushed for 60 yards and two scores on 20 carries, adding three receptions for 19 yards and another touchdown in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Montgomery was given 23 touches in his debut with the Texans, as the veteran back was a focal point of the offense. Granted, he only averaged 3.0 yards per carry, but he found the end zone three times while being involved both on the ground and through the air.

news.head: David Montgomery traded to Houston Texans
news.body: David Montgomery has been traded to the Houston Texans. Houston is sending a fourth rounder, OL Juice Scruggs, and a seventh back to Detroit.
news.impact: Montgomery had made it known he wanted a new opportunity given his lack of usage last year, and the Texans came calling. Monty offers a big upgrade over Nick Chubb as the primary thumper, and his ability in the passing game could easily endanger Woody Marks value as well. For dynasty, it’s great for Montgomery and Jahmyr Gibbs managers, while Marks managers will have to deal with a much bigger threat to any potential volume. This also likely means Joe Mixon, who missed all of last season, is done in Houston.

news.head: David Montgomery gets eight carries in Week 18
news.body: David Montgomery carried the ball eight times for 42 yards and added one catch for 13 yards in Detroit's win over Chicago on Sunday.
news.impact: Montgomery has seen his production drop over the last couple of seasons as Jahmyr Gibbs has emerged as the lead back for the Lions. The seventh-year running back still had a solid campaign with 158 carries for 716 yards and eight scores. However, the carries and the rushing yards were new career-lows for Montgomery.

news.head: David Montgomery quiet in Week 17 loss
news.body: David Montgomery rushed 10 times for 25 yards while also catching both of his targets for 15 yards in the Lions' 23-10 loss to the Vikings in Week 17.
news.impact: Montgomery has struggled to make an impact out of the Detroit backfield of late, finishing with 40 or less offensive yards in each of his last three games. The running back remains a difficult option for fantasy managers to trust in any format ahead of a Week 18 matchup against the Chicago Bears.

news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba electric in win Wednesday
news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 8-of-11 targets for 122 yards and a touchdown in Wednesday night's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.impact: On Wednesday, Smith-Njigba picked up right where he left off last season, exploding for 122 yards and a touchdown in a big win over the Patriots. He did that with Drew Lock throwing him passes after starter Sam Darnold went down with a hip injury earlier in the game. Fantasy managers should be happy with his performance in this matchup but should keep a close eye on the health of Darnold, as the young wideout's week-to-week ceiling will certainly take a hit if their starting QB misses significant time.

news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba signs historic four-year extension with Seahawks
news.body: The Seahawks signed WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba to a four-year, $168.6 million contract extension.
news.impact: Smith-Njigba signs the richest contract extension for a receiver in NFL history with the deal including $120 million in guaranteed money. The 2025 NFL Offensive Player of the Year and Super Bowl Champion went for 1,793 yards and 10 touchdowns on 119 receptions last season. He will remain under contract with the Seahawks through the 2031 season.

news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has fifth-year team option exercised by Seahawks
news.body: The Seahawks exercised WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s fifth-year team option for 2027.
news.impact: Henderson added that Smith-Njigba’s 2027 salary is fully guaranteed and should make him roughly $23.85 million. This is expected to be a step towards the two sides agreeing to a long-term extension.

news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba off injury report for Super Bowl
news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is off the injury report for the Super Bowl against the Patriots.
news.impact: Smith-Njigba closed the week with a full practice on Friday. He is officially a full-go heading into the big game on Sunday.

news.head: Colston Loveland sees two targets in Week 1
news.body: Colston Loveland failed to catch either of his two targets in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Loveland was non-existent in an explosive Chicago offense for head coach Ben Johnson in the season opener, operating as more of an afterthought in the win. The tight end will look to get back on track in a Week 2 divisional contest against the Minnesota Vikings.

news.head: Colston Loveland catches 10 passes and scores TD in Week 18
news.body: Colston Loveland caught a team-high 10 passes, on 13 targets, for 91 yards and a score in the Bears' 19-16 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
news.impact: Loveland, the first-round pick out of Michigan, is starting to get hot at the right time for the Bears. Over the last two weeks, the tight end has caught 16 passes for 185 yards and two touchdowns. After a slow start to the season (11 catches in the first six weeks), Loveland has caught 47 passes over his last ten games. He will look to remain a focal point of the offense during the postseason.

news.head: Colston Loveland sees 10 targets in Week 17 loss to 49ers
news.body: Colston Loveland hauled in six of his team-leading 10 targets for 94 yards and one touchdown in the Bears' 42-38 Week 17 loss to the 49ers.
news.impact: Loveland has made the most of modest involvement in the Chicago passing attack of late, recording one touchdown in three of his last six games. The tight end remains a boom-or-bust tight end option in all formats for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 18 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

news.head: Colston Loveland hauls in three receptions in Week 16 win
news.body: Colston Loveland hauled in three of his four targets for 30 yards in the Bears' 22-16 Week 16 win over the Packers.
news.impact: Loveland has struggled to make a consistent impact in the Chicago passing attack, finishing with less than 50 receiving yards in five of his last six games. The tight end remains a difficult option for fantasy managers to trust ahead of a Week 17 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

news.head: Tetairoa McMillan hauls in five receptions in Week 1 loss
news.body: Tetairoa McMillan hauled in five of his eight targets for 75 yards in the Panthers' 59-37 Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: McMillan made the most of his sizeable volume in the Carolina passing attack, finishing second in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the loss. The wideout remains one of the more dynamic pass-catching options in the Carolina offense moving forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.head: Tetairoa McMillan (foot) practices Thursday
news.body: Tetairoa McMillan was at practice on Thursday.
news.impact: The Panthers and Cardinals are the first teams to have veterans report to training camp. McMillan had missed most of the spring due to a foot injury.

news.head: Tetairoa McMillan expected to see more slot usage this season
news.body: Cameron Wolfe reports that Tetairoa McMillan is expected to see more usage in the slot this season.
news.impact: McMillan started to see more snaps in the slot during the second half of his rookie season last year. Wolfe notes that the Panthers believe Chris Brazzell II will be able to play on the outside that will allow McMillan the opportunity to play more in the slot. He should be able to take advantage of mismatches in the slot as he looks to take a step forward heading into his second season in the NFL.

news.head: Tetairoa McMillan (ankle) hopeful to be ready for training camp
news.body: Tetairoa McMillan told reporters he is hopeful to be ready for the start of training camp.
news.impact: McMillan has been limited to individual drills early on in OTAs. He said he is "feeling better" now.

news.head: KC Concepcion snags four passes in loss to Jags
news.body: KC Concepcion caught four of five targets for 43 yards in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars. He also ran the ball three times for 15 yards.
news.impact: While it wasn't a massive day, it was encouraging that Concepcion got touches as both a receiver and out of the backfield, showing the team wanted to get the ball in his hands. A loss is a loss, but brighter days should be ahead for Concepcion.

news.head: KC Concepcion (shoulder) returns to practice Tuesday
news.body: KC Concepcion was back at practice on Tuesday at Browns training camp.
news.impact: Concepcion landed hard on his shoulder that forced him out of Monday's practice early. He is back one day later.

news.head: KC Concepcion (shoulder) avoids serious injury
news.body: Browns rookie WR KC Concepcion is believed to have avoided a serious shoulder injury on Monday.
news.impact: Concepcion left practice on Monday with a shoulder injury after a hard fall. The team expects him to be fine.

news.head: KC Concepcion (knee) medically cleared
news.body: Browns coach Todd Monken said KC Concepcion has been cleared medically and is good to go.
news.impact: Concepcion participated in individual and team drills on Friday. He had a knee scope in March, which led to the team monitoring his reps previously.

news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. goes for 58 yards in Week 1
news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. caught all three of his targets for 58 yards in a 20-13 win over the Falcons in Week 1.
news.impact: Pittman led the Steelers in receiving despite only seeing three targets. It was a slightly concerning Pittsburgh debut for the veteran, as DK Metcalf easily dominated in the target category, drawing 10. Pittman will be a fantasy flex option heading into Week 2 against the Patriots but should be on the bench if there are better starting options available.

news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (hamstring) good to go for Sunday
news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. (hamstring) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.
news.impact: Pittman is now fully recovered from the hamstring injury he was dealing with earlier and is set to be a full go against the Falcons on Sunday. He shouldn't be started in most league formats but remains an intriguing player to watch and evaluate in his first game as a member of his new team.

news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (hamstring) practices Monday
news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. practiced on Monday.
news.impact: Pittman missed time during training camp with a hamstring injury. He remains on track to be good to go for Sunday's season opener against the Falcons.

news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. will be available Week 1
news.body: Steelers GM Omar Khan announced WR Michael Pittman Jr. will be available for Week 1.
news.impact: Pittman has been dealing with a hamstring injury, but will still suit up in Week 1. He slots in as a low-end flex play in his Steelers debut against the Falcons.

news.head: Matthew Golden totals 95 yards Sunday
news.body: Matthew Golden caught 6-of-12 targets for 95 yards in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings.
news.impact: After a lost rookie season, Golden opened this year leading Green Bay receivers in targets on Sunday. He is in the WR3/WR4 mix heading into Week 2 for fantasy managers.

news.head: Matthew Golden (toe) returns to practice Tuesday
news.body: Matthew Golden was back at practice at Packers training camp on Tuesday.
news.impact: Golden makes his way back after missing a few days of practice. He was spotted running with the Green Bay first team offense on Tuesday.

news.head: Matthew Golden (toe) not expected to practice Monday
news.body: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said he does not expect WR Matthew Golden to practice on Monday.
news.impact: Golden also missed practice on Sunday. He remains day-to-day. It is unknown how serious his injury is.

news.head: Matthew Golden (toe) not practicing Sunday
news.body: Matthew Golden did not practice on Sunday due to a toe injury.
news.impact: It is unclear how serious the injury is for Golden. He is day-to-day going into the week. There should be an update provided by coach Matt LaFleur when available.

news.head: Tyjae Spears finishes with 24 all-purpose yards in Week 1
news.body: Tyjae Spears carried the ball three times for 12 yards and caught two of his four targets for 12 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
news.impact: Spears operated behind Tony Pollard, who had eight touches. It was not a great day for the Tennessee run game, as the Titans were playing from behind for the entire game. Spears at least drew an encouraging number of targets in the passing attack. He will be a low-end flex option heading into Week 2 against the Eagles.

news.head: Tyjae Spears racks up seven receptions in loss
news.body: Tyjae Spears ran three times for 18 yards and caught all seven of his targets for nine yards in the Titans' 41-7 loss to the Jaguars.
news.impact: Spears made his fantasy day with his receiving in PPR leagues, but the yards certainly didn't come with it. His nine yards were the fewest yards on seven catches since at least 2010. Spears has some PPR appeal, but in a split backfield, it's tough to see him as much more than a flex play in 2026.

news.head: Tyjae Spears does nothing with seven touches Sunday
news.body: Tyjae Spears gained only two yards on six carries and negative yardage on one catch in Sunday's loss to the Saints.
news.impact: After putting up his best game of the season in Week 16, Spears let down any fantasy managers who took a shot on him in Week 17. He is a real long shot to do much of anything against the Jaguars' tenacious run defense in Week 18.

news.head: Tyjae Spears finds the end zone Sunday
news.body: Tyjae Spears ran for 52 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries in the Titans 26-9 win over the Chiefs. He also caught 5-of-5 targets for 53 yards receiving.
news.impact: Spears totaled over 100 yards from scrimmage with a score. He had a long catch and run of 34 yards. He'll be on the low-end flex radar next week against the Saints.

news.head: Zach Charbonnet (knee) has 'aggressive' return timeline
news.body: Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet has an "aggressive" timeline for his return from injury, says head coach Mike Macdonald.
news.impact: Charbonnet is opening the season on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list. He will miss at least four games, but he could be off the PUP list sooner than expected. Macdonald did not disclose specifics on Charbonnet's timeline. The fourth-year running back has scored 20 rushing touchdowns in the last two seasons and tore his ACL in January.

news.head: Zach Charbonnet (knee) placed on PUP list
news.body: The Seahawks placed Zach Charbonnet on the PUP list.
news.impact: Charbonnet will miss at least the first four games of the season. Rookie RB Jadarian Price will open the year as the lead back with George Holani behind him.

news.head: Zach Charbonnet (knee) placed on PUP list
news.body: The Seahawks officially placed RB Zach Charbonnet on the PUP list.
