news.body: The Lions D/ST forced three turnovers (two interceptions, one fumble recovery) while also picking up five sacks in a 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.impact: The unit escaped after allowing the Saints to come back from a 21-0 deficit in the second half, with New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough overthrowing a potential game-winning two-point conversion in overtime. Fantasy managers will need to have another option available with a Week 2 matchup against the Buffalo Bills up next.

news.head: Detroit Lions D/ST quiet in season finale
news.body: The Detroit Lions D/ST recorded just one sack and had one interception during the team's 19-16 win over the Bears in the last game of the year.
news.impact: The Lions allowed only 270 yards of total offense to the Bears, marking the sixth-lowest total they have allowed in a game all season. However, they had trouble getting to Caleb Williams, sacking the quarterback just once. Avonte Maddox had the interception which led to a Lions' field goal late in the third quarter.

news.head: Lions D/ST records seven sacks in Week 17
news.body: The Lions D/ST recorded seven sacks while failing to force any turnovers in a 23-10 loss to the Vikings in Week 17.
news.impact: The unit fell victim to a turnover-heavy performance from the offense as the defense made stops for the most part when needed. Fantasy managers should look for alternatives in all formats ahead of a Week 18 contest against the Chicago Bears.

news.head: Lions D/ST struggles against run Sunday
news.body: The Lions D/ST allowed 29 points on 481 total yards with two sacks and one fumble recovery on Sunday against the Steelers.
news.impact: Jaylen Warren ripped off a pair of long touchdown runs in the final quarter. Detroit did recover one fumble lost by Darnell Washington, but it was a rough second half for them as a unit.

news.head: Pat Freiermuth finds the end zone in Week 1 win
news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught all five of his targets for 46 yards and a touchdown in a 20-13 win over the Falcons in Week 1.
news.impact: Freiermuth kicked off the season with a promising outing in the win over Atlanta. He hauled in Aaron Rodgers' lone touchdown pass on a six-yard catch in the second quarter while tying for second on the team in receptions. Freiermuth will settle in as a TE2 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots.

news.head: Pat Freiermuth goes for 51 yards in Week 18
news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught three of his five targets for 51 yards in a 26-24 win over the Ravens in Week 18.
news.impact: Freiermuth finished third on the Steelers in receiving in the win. The veteran tight end wraps the regular season with 41 catches for 486 yards and four touchdowns while appearing in all 17 of the Steelers' games. He will now prepare to take on the Texans at home in the Wild-Card round of the playoffs.

news.head: Pat Freiermuth hauls in three passes in Week 17
news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught 3-of-5 targets for 63 yards in the Steelers 13-6 loss to the Browns.
news.impact: Freiermuth saw an increase in targets after Darnell Washington exited the game with a broken arm. With Washington out next week, Freiermuth and Jonnu Smith should see the bulk of the snaps at tight end against the Ravens in a matchup with the Ravens to decide the AFC North.

news.head: Pat Freiermuth catches four passes Sunday
news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught 4-of-4 targets for 20 yards in the Steelers 29-24 win over the Lions.
news.impact: Freiermuth finished the day tied for second on the team in receptions. He remains off the fantasy radar.

news.head: Justice Hill sees seven touches in Week 1
news.body: Justice Hill rushed six times for 18 yards while catching his only target for 10 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1.
news.impact: Hill operated as more of an afterthought out of the Baltimore backfield, with Derrick Henry and Lamar Jackson finishing ahead of the running back in carries. He remains more of a change-of-pace option behind Henry ahead of a Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

news.head: Justice Hill (neck) to miss 3-to-4 weeks
news.body: Ravens coach John Harbaugh said Justice Hill will be out three to four weeks with a neck injury.
news.impact: Hill will miss at least the next few weeks. He'll have a chance to still return this season.

news.head: Justice Hill (toe) could return this season
news.body: Ravens coach John Harbaugh said RB Justice Hill could return this season.
news.impact: Harbaugh noted that Hill has a three-or-four week injury. He remains off the fantasy radar.

news.head: Justice Hill (toe) ruled out for Week 13
news.body: Justice Hill has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Bengals.
news.impact: Hill was added to the injury report on Tuesday. Keaton Mitchell will continue to see snaps behind Derrick Henry.

news.head: Makai Lemon quiet in Week 1
news.body: Makai Lemon caught three of his four targets for a loss of five yards on the Eagles’ 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders in Week 1.
news.impact: Lemon struggled to find any success in the season opener, as the pass-catcher was bottled up by the Commanders defense in the win. The wideout will look for more impactful output in a favorable Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

news.head: Makai Lemon (hamstring) practicing in full on Monday
news.body: Makai Lemon (hamstring) is back to practicing fully for the first time in weeks. He returned to practice in a limited fashion last week, and is now practicing in full.
news.impact: This is huge for Lemon’s development and integration into the offense. The more reps he gets, especially as a rookie, the better. He’s looking like a potential draft steal if he can continue to stay healthy and improve his game.

news.head: Makai Lemon (hamstring) limited at practice Thursday
news.body: Makai Lemon (hamstring) was limited at Philadelphia's practice on Thursday.
news.impact: The rookie was able to make his return to practice on Thursday. He was sidelined for a little while after suffering a hamstring injury, but it seems that he is progressing well with his recovery, as the team is now letting him practice in a limited capacity. At this rate he will be ready to play in time for the team's season opener, barring any setbacks with his recovery.

news.head: Makai Lemon (hamstring) still not practicing Wednesday
news.body: Makai Lemon remained absent from practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Lemon has been sidelined for nearly two weeks with the hamstring issue. It remains unclear when he will return to practice.

news.head: Bo Nix struggles in loss Monday
news.body: Bo Nix completed 17-of-28 passing attempts for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: Nix had a poor performance on Monday night. He was held to just 131 passing yards on the night and wasn't able to get Denver's offense going, leading them to score just ten points en route to a blowout loss at the hands of their divisional rivals. He should improve and play better in more favorable matchups moving forward, but they will continue to have a tough schedule for the foreseeable future, so fantasy managers might be better off looking for another option for the time being.

news.head: Bo Nix will not play in preseason opener
news.body: Bo Nix will not play in the Broncos preseason opener against the Falcons.
news.impact: Nix is expected to play in the second and third preseason games. Jarrett Stidham and Sam Ehlinger will both play a half.

news.head: Bo Nix (ankle) practices without limitations Wednesday
news.body: Bo Nix practiced on Wednesday at Broncos training camp without any limitations.
news.impact: Nix was able to get 7-on-7 work in during OTAs. He appears to be well on track to be good to go for the start of the season.

news.head: Bo Nix (ankle) participates in 7-on-7 drills Wednesday
news.body: Broncos QB Bo Nix participated in the 7-on-7 periods during the team’s second minicamp practice Wednesday.
news.impact: Per Kosmider, Nix hit RJ Harvey for a touchdown during a red-zone drill. He remains on track to be a full-go for training camp.

news.head: Chris Olave surpasses 180 receiving yards in Week 1 loss to Lions
news.body: Chris Olave hauled in 10 of his team-leading 13 targets for 182 receiving yards in the Saints' 31-30 Week 1 loss to the Detroit Lions.
news.impact: Olave capitalized on a dynamic role in the New Orleans passing attack for head coach Kellen Moore, averaging 18.2 yards per reception while leading the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the loss. The wideout remains a steady WR1 option for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 2 contest against the Baltimore Ravens.

news.head: Chris Olave slow to get up Tuesday at practice
news.body: Chris Olave was slow to get up after doing a deep route in practice, landing hard on his back. HC Kellen Moore said that the receiver had the wind knocked out of him, and when asked if there would be further tests or cause for concern, declined to answer.
news.impact: It sounds like Olave should be fine. He shouldn’t suffer any setbacks because of this unless the staff is hiding details. Draft Olave with confidence as the WR1 in an up and coming Saints offense.

news.head: Chris Olave takes part in team drills Friday
news.body: Chris Olave took part in team drills at practice on Friday at Saints training camp.
news.impact: Olave was limited to individual drills earlier in the week. With his extension now out of the way, he'll now fully participate in practices.

news.head: Chris Olave agrees to four-year, $132 million extension with Saints
news.body: Chris Olave has agreed to a four-year, $132 million extension with the New Orleans Saints, including $90 million guaranteed.
news.impact: Olave had a big 2025 season, and it paid off beautifully for the veteran receiver. He’s now locked in for the long haul in a promising situation in New Orleans with a breakout QB in Tyler Shough, and new additions Travis Etienne and Jordyn Tyson.

news.head: Kenneth Walker III dominant in win Monday
news.body: Kenneth Walker III rushed the ball 23 times for 173 yards and a touchdown while catching 3-of-6 targets for 18 yards and an additional touchdown in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Walker was absolutely dominant in his debut with the Chiefs on Monday night. He totaled 191 yards and two touchdowns over the course of the game, which was especially impressive considering that he did it against one of the best defenses in the NFL in the Broncos. He looks great on his new offense and should be in line for a huge season if he can stay healthy with this increased workload.

news.head: Kenneth Walker III (foot) off injury report for Monday
news.body: Kenneth Walker III (foot) is off of the injury report ahead of Monday night's game against the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Walker was previously dealing with a foot injury of some kind, but he is over it now and is no longer listed on the team's injury report ahead of their Week 1 matchup against the Broncos. Fantasy managers should expect him to be highly involved on Monday night, although the tough matchup may hurt his ceiling from a fantasy perspective.

news.head: Kenneth Walker III (foot) not practicing Tuesday
news.body: Kenneth Walker III is not practicing on Tuesday due to a foot injury.
news.impact: It is unclear how serious the injury is for Walker. His status will need to be monitored in practice the rest of the week.

news.head: Kenneth Walker III primed for 'workhorse' role
news.body: Kenneth Walker III is reportedly "primed to be the clear workhorse" in the Chiefs' offense.
news.impact: Walker is currently being selected as a low-end RB1 in fantasy drafts. If the Chiefs rely on him as reported, though, Walker has a strong chance to finish as a top-five RB.

news.head: Josh Downs catches two passes in Week 1
news.body: Josh Downs caught two of his four targets for 37 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
news.impact: Downs saw modest involvement in an underperforming Indianapolis passing attack, finishing third on the team in targets in the loss. The wideout remains one of the more risky pass-catchers entering a difficult Week 2 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.head: Josh Downs (calf) without injury designation for Sunday
news.body: Josh Downs (calf) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens.
news.impact: Downs is not listed on Indianapolis' injury report heading into Week 1, meaning that his calf injury is no longer an issue and that he should be at full health at this point. Indianapolis' distribution of targets should be something fantasy managers keep a close eye on this weekend, but the 25-year old isn't projected to be a strong fantasy asset on his own to start the season.

news.head: Josh Downs (calf) practices Tuesday
news.body: Josh Downs practiced on Tuesday.
news.impact: Downs missed time last week with a calf issue. He is on track to be good to go for the season opener next week.

news.head: Josh Downs (calf) not practicing Wednesday
news.body: Josh Downs did not practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Downs missed practice for undisclosed reasons on Tuesday and it is now said to be a calf injury. He remains day-to-day.

news.head: Chuba Hubbard scores two touchdowns in Week 1 loss to Bears
news.body: Chuba Hubbard carried the ball 10 times for 49 yards and one touchdown while also catching all three of his targets for 38 yards and one touchdown in the Panthers' 59-37 Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: Hubbard took advantage of a primary ball-carrying option before the game script changed, leading the team in rushing yards in the loss. The running back remains a solid option out of the backfield for head coach Dave Canales, with a Week 2 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.head: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) off injury report for Week 1
news.body: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) is off of the injury report ahead of Week 1's matchup against the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: Hubbard was battling a hamstring injury earlier this offseason, but it's no longer an issue for him and he carries no injury designation ahead of Week 1. He will likely split work with Jonathan Brooks (groin) in the season opener, which hurts the fantasy outlook for both of them.

news.head: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) week-to-week with hamstring injury
news.body: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) is week-to-week with a hamstring injury per HC Dave Canales. He is expected to play in Week 1.
news.impact: While it sounds like Hubbard should be good to go for the season opener, he could still be limited following a multi-week absence. With that said, it’s now wheels up for Jonathon Brooks, who’s now going to see his ADP rise yet again.

news.head: Chuba Hubbard to play in preseason game Saturday
news.body: Chuba Hubbard will play in the Panthers preseason game on Saturday against the Bills.
news.impact: Hubbard is unlikely to see many snaps. The Panthers are also expected to play Jonathon Brooks.

news.head: Zay Flowers (hamstring) considered day-to-day
news.body: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said WR Zay Flowers is considered day-to-day with a hamstring injury.
news.impact: It is a good sign after Flowers left Sunday's game early after a very strong first half. His status for Week 2 still remains uncertain.

news.head: Zay Flowers (hamstring) ruled out Sunday
news.body: Zay Flowers (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of the Week 1 contest between the Baltimore Ravens and Indianapolis Colts according to Mike Garafolo.
news.impact: Flowers had been sidelined since the second quarter while attempting to work through the hamstring injury an return for head coach Jesse Minter, hauling in five of his six targets for 150 receiving yards and one touchdown on the day.

news.head: Zay Flowers (hamstring) questionable to return Sunday
news.body: Zay Flowers (hamstring) is questionable to return for the Baltimore Ravens against the Indianapolis Colts Sunday the organization announced.
news.impact: Flowers was off to a dynamic start before leaving in the second quarter for head coach Jesse Minter, hauling in five of his six targets for 150 receiving yards and one touchdown prior to exiting. Rashod Bateman and Ja’Kobi Lane would see increased targets if the superstar wideout remains sidelined in the second half for the Ravens.

news.head: Zay Flowers (hamstring) off injury report Sunday
news.body: Zay Flowers is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Colts.
news.impact: Flowers missed some practice time in the past couple of weeks with a hamstring injury. He'll be a full-go heading into the season off a new contract.

news.head: Courtland Sutton uninvolved in loss Monday
news.body: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-5 targets for just 11 yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: Denver's offense as a whole struggled heavily on Monday night, and Sutton was no exception to that. He caught just two of his five targets over the course of the game and was only able to turn that into a measly 11 yards. He remains off of the fantasy radar for the foreseeable future, even in more favorable matchups.

news.head: Courtland Sutton in full pads at practice Friday
news.body: Courtland Sutton was seen in full pads to begin practice on Friday.
news.impact: It is a positive sign after Sutton missed practice on Tuesday and Wednesday before he was limited in his return on Thursday. It appears he should be able to do more in practice on Friday.

news.head: Courtland Sutton being limited early in training camp
news.body: Broncos WR Courtland Sutton is “being limited as part of the team’s ‘protocols’ for the veteran wide receiver.”
news.impact: It explains why Sutton was not seen practicing on Tuesday or Wednesday. He returned to practice on Thursday, but he was still held out of team drills. He should continue to be ramped up as we get closer to the season.

news.head: Courtland Sutton to return to practice Thursday
news.body: Broncos coach Sean Payton said WR Courtland Sutton will return to practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Sutton did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday which raised some concern. Payton listed it as "intentional load management" for Sutton.

news.head: Alec Pierce suffers hand/wrist bruise, expected to be fine
news.body: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce’s left hand/wrist is fine.
news.impact: Pierce said he is dealing with a bruise. His status will need to be monitored in practice this week.

news.head: Alec Pierce leads pass-catchers in Week 1 loss
news.body: Alec Pierce hauled in four of his team-leading six targets for 61 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Ravens in Week 1.
news.impact: Pierce was impactful for head coach Shane Steichen while operating on a snap count, leading the Colts in targets and receiving yards in a losing effort. The wideout remains an impactful pass-catching option ahead of a tough Week 2 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.head: Alec Pierce (heel) on snap count for Week 1
news.body: Alec Pierce (heel) will operate on a snap count in Week 1 for the Indianapolis Colts against the Baltimore Ravens according to Mike Garafolo.
news.impact: Pierce is in line for 20-60 plays according to Garafolo as the wideout continues to work back towards full health after a late start to his preseason activities for the Colts. Tight end Tyler Warren alongside wideouts Keenan Allen and Josh Downs will likely see increased targets from quarterback Daniel Jones against the Ravens Sunday.

news.head: Alec Pierce (heel) off injury report Sunday
news.body: Alec Pierce is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
news.impact: Pierce is not expected to face a snap count. He is fresh off his contract extension this offseason.

news.head: Patrick Mahomes II scores three touchdowns in return game Monday
news.body: Patrick Mahomes II completed 15-of-27 passing attempts for 184 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception while adding 23 yards and a touchdown on the ground in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Monday night marked Mahomes' first game back after suffering a serious knee injury that ended his 2025 season prematurely. He looked good in his first game back, totaling over 200 yards and scoring three touchdowns on the night, including one impressive rushing touchdown from over ten yards out. He and Kansas City's offense as a whole are looking promising right now and may be primed for a big season if they can stay healthy this year.

news.head: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) active for Week 1
news.body: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) is active for Week 1 for the Kansas City Chiefs against the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Mahomes II cleared through every obstacle in his way in recovering from a late-season knee injury in 2025-26, as the dynamic signal-caller looks to lead a revamped Kansas City offense back to the postseason beginning with the Week 1 divisional matchup against a disruptive Denver defense Monday night.

news.head: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) practices in full Thursday
news.body: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) practiced in a full capacity on Thursday.
news.impact: Mahomes was able to take part in Kansas City's first practice of the week on Thursday and wasn't limited in any way. It seems like the team is planning on him starting on Monday night, barring any unforeseen setbacks. His presence would be great news for the fantasy value of players like Rashee Rice and Travis Kelce in a matchup against a tough Denver defense.

news.head: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) to start Week 1 barring setback
news.body: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Patrick Mahomes is set to start on Monday night barring a setback.
news.impact: Mahomes has officially worked his way back from a torn ACL and LCL suffered in Week 15 last year. He has said he may not run as much coming off the injury, at least early in the season.

news.head: Matthew Stafford quiet in loss to Niners
news.body: Matthew Stafford completed 15-of-25 passes for 155 yards and a pick in the Rams' 27-7 blowout loss to the 49ers. He also ran twice for a loss of a yard.
news.impact: Stafford was not in his best form on Thursday, missing throws and looking a little rusty. It's a rough start for a team that was deemed Super Bowl-bound, but he will look to get back on track next week.

news.head: Matthew Stafford expected to have reps managed in training camp
news.body: The Rams are expected to limit the reps for Matthew Stafford in training camp.
news.impact: Stafford’s degenerative back issue cost him almost all of training camp last year, and he went on to have an MVP season. He is expected to have load managment once again throughout training camp as he enters another season.

news.head: Matthew Stafford agrees to one-year, $55 million extension
news.body: Matthew Stafford has agreed to a one-year, $55 million extension with the Rams. He is now under contract for LA for the next two seasons.
news.impact: The Rams are in a Super Bowl window, so this is hardly a surprising move. Stafford will give them the boost they need off of an MVP season to help them continue to compete for the next two years. As for Ty Simpson, it looks like he will be on the Jordan Love trajectory where we will need to wait at least two years to really get a shot as a starter.

news.head: Matthew Stafford, Rams deep in contract extension talks
news.body: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Matthew Stafford and the Rams are “deep” in contract extension talks.
news.impact: Rapoport added that the Rams believe there is a “real chance” Stafford plays beyond the 2026 season. This comes the day after they invested the No. 13 overall pick on Ty Simpson. It appears he is likely to be sitting multiple years behind Stafford.

news.head: Evan Engram hauls in touchdown Monday
news.body: Evan Engram caught 4-f-5 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: Engram was one of Denver's lone bright spots on offense on Monday night. He caught all but one of his targets against the Chiefs, including one that accounted for the Broncos' lone touchdown in this matchup. He isn't expected to be fantasy relevant moving forward, however, and should remain on the waiver wire in most leagues.

news.head: Evan Engram could take on bigger role next season per Broncos GM
news.body: Broncos GM George Paton said the team wants to add to TE Evan Engram’s workload next year.
news.impact: It is also worth noting that Denver has been linked to the top tight end prospects in next week's draft. That will need to be monitored to get a better idea of Engram's role heading into next season.

news.head: Evan Engram leads team in receiving Sunday
news.body: Evan Engram caught 3-of-4 targets for 45 yards in Sunday's 19-3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: The veteran finished as the team's leading receiver on Sunday, despite only racking up a modest 45 yards over the course of the game. He should continue to be an important part of Denver's offense as they now head into the postseason.

news.head: Evan Engram catches four passes in Thursday's win
news.body: Evan Engram secured all four of his targets for 21 yards in Thursday's win over the Chiefs.
news.impact: Engram actually doubled his catch total from Week 16, but he didn't manage much in the yardage department, serving basically as a safety blanket for QB Bo Nix on Thursday. Engram is regularly involved in the Broncos' passing game, but his fantasy upside has been significantly capped over the last few weeks. In his last four games, the veteran TE has topped out at 36 yards with no touchdowns.

news.head: Jaxson Dart electric in win Sunday
news.body: Jaxson Dart completed 23-of-29 passing attempts for 230 yards and three touchdowns while adding 54 yards on the ground in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.impact: Dart had a great start to the season on Sunday night. He totaled close to 300 yards and three touchdowns in a big win over the Cowboys, and he didn't lose any turnovers in the process. New York's offense as a whole looked effective with him at the helm, and they will likely continue to look good for the next three or four weeks with a relatively easy schedule coming down the pipe.

news.head: Jaxson Dart focusing on mature scrambling decisions
news.body: Giants QB Jaxson Dart said he won't change competitiveness but is focusing on mature scrambling decisions.
news.impact: Dart suffered multiple concussions last season, in large part due to how often he scrambled and ran the ball. He'll likely attempt to slide sooner when necessary this season. He should still provide plenty of rushing upside for fantasy managers.

news.head: Jaxson Dart finishes rookie season with a solid effort
news.body: Jaxson Dart completed 22 of 32 passes for 230 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions, adding 32 yards on five carries in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Cowboys.
news.impact: Dart wrapped up his rookie campaign with yet another promising performance at the helm of the Giants offense. The former Ole Miss standout has given the Giants plenty of confidence build around him for the future. Over 14 games this season, Dart completed 63.2% of his passes for 2,272 yards and 15-5 TD/INT ratio. He also used his running ability to gain nearly 500 yards and account for another nine touchdowns. Dart is an extremely valuable dynasty or keeper-league piece, and he is sure to have his suitors in 2026 redraft formats as well.

news.head: Jaxson Dart: Giants starters expected to play in Week 18
news.body: Giants interim coach Mike Kafka plans to stick with his usual starters for New York in Week 18 against the Cowboys.
news.impact: Dak Prescott is expected to play, so both teams starters should play in the season finale for both teams. It is a favorable matchup for Dart and the Giants offense to end the season on a high note.

news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. held without a catch in Week 1
news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. failed to catch his lone target in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1.
news.impact: It was a rough day for the Atlanta passing attack as third-string QB Cooper Rush only passed for 143 yards. Pitts will hope to bounce back in Week 2 against the Panthers, although he will be tough to trust in fantasy as long as Rush is under center.

news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. agrees to 3-year, $54 million extension with Falcons
news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. has agreed to a 3-year, $54 million extension with the Atlanta Falcons.
news.impact: After coming off arguably his best season as a pro, Pitts gets the bag. He will operate as the teams second target behind Drake London and TE1 in a tight end friendly Stefanski system. It’s wheels up for the still young Pitts.

news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. could be moved if Falcons find trade partner
news.body: Adam Schefter said “he would watch to see if [the Falcons] could find a trade partner for Kyle Pitts, who they’re open to dealing.”
news.impact: Pitts had found himself in the midst of trade rumors earlier in the offseason, but they have quieted down since. He signed his franchise tender earlier in April. It still seems like Pitts will likely remain in Atlanta, but it is at least worth monitoring.

news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. showing up for Falcons voluntary offseason workouts
news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. is signing his franchise tag and showing up for the Falcons voluntary workouts to begin their offseason program.
news.impact: The two sides can still negotiate a long-term deal. The tag is $15.045 million fully guaranteed. Pitts took a step forward in his career last season, most notably when Drake London missed time.

news.head: Jeremiyah Love finds the end zone in debut
news.body: Jeremiyah Love picked up 41 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.impact: Love added a pair of grabs for nine yards to his NFL debut, and despite still being somewhat limited by the ankle sprain he sustained a month ago, the rookie certainly showed promise of things to come. Tyler Allgeier did get six more carries than Love, but that load share should begin to swing the other way as the season moves forward. The Cardinals have a tough matchup with the Seahawks on tap for Week 2.

news.head: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) active for Week 1
news.body: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is active for Week 1 for the Arizona Cardinals against the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: Love is good to go after clearing through pregame activities without any setbacks from the injured ankle, with the rookie running back set to share the backfield with free agent Tyler Allgeier against the Chargers.

news.head: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) expected to play on Sunday against Chargers
news.body: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is expected to play against the Chargers on Sunday.
news.impact: Love is currently listed as questionable, but barring a setback, looks like he will be good to go against the Chargers. While his talent is among the best in the league, his role might be limited as he continues to work his way back from injury. Expect closer to RB3 numbers with upside for much more.

news.head: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) officially questionable for Sunday
news.body: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: The rookie is officially being listed as questionable to play in Sunday's season opener. There have been a lot of optimistic reports surrounding his availability, so it looks more likely than not that he will suit up against the Chargers, although that decision won't be made until closer to game time. If he is ruled out, Tyler Allgeier will be primed for a massive workload in Week 1 in Love's absence.

news.head: Rome Odunze quiet in Week 1
news.body: Rome Odunze caught two of his three targets for 52 yards in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers
news.impact: Odunze made the most of minimal usage in the Chicago passing attack in the season opener, averaging 26.0 yards per reception in the win. the wideout provides head coach Ben Johnson with one of many dynamic pass-catching options ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

news.head: Rome Odunze (calf) active for Week 1
news.body: Rome Odunze (calf) is officially active for Week 1 for the Chicago Bears against the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Odunze is good to go after passing through pregame testing without any setbacks from the calf injury, offering head coach Ben Johnson another dynamic pass-catching option for quarterback Caleb Williams against the Panthers Sunday.

news.head: Rome Odunze (calf) expected to play against Carolina
news.body: Rome Odunze (calf) is expected to play against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.
news.impact: The Bears made several receiver moves on Saturday, bringing doubt to Odunze's status. However, it does look like the young receiver will play. He's worth starting, but temper expectations a little.

news.head: Rome Odunze (calf) questionable to play Sunday
news.body: Rome Odunze (calf) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Odunze has been limited at practice all week due to a calf injury, and now it is threatening to leave him sidelined for the team's season opener on Sunday. He is officially considered questionable to play, and the team will make a final determination about his availability closer to game time. Luther Burden III will be a great fantasy option if Odunze is ruled out, with Zavion Thomas also likely to step up and see more work.

news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. hauls in four passes Sunday
news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. caught 4-of-4 targets for 40 yards in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.impact: Godwin totaled 30 of his 40 yards on one reception. The Bucs offense was unable to get in sync with four lost fumbles. He'll remain a WR3 heading into Week 2 against the Browns.

news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. (soreness) does not practice Tuesday
news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. did not practice on Tuesday to manage injuries and soreness.
news.impact: Godwin, Jalen McMillan and Emeka Egbuka all sat out on Tuesday. It doesn't appear to be anything serious with any of them.

news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. quiet in Week 18
news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. caught his lone target for eight yards in the Bucs 16-14 win over the Panthers.
news.impact: It was a quiet day for the entire Bucs wide receiver room. Godwin showed flashes after working his way back to full health, but he struggled to finish the season. He'll be a bounce back candidate next year.

news.head: Chris Godwin (illness) questionable, will play Saturday
news.body: Chris Godwin (illness) will be available for Saturday's game.
news.impact: Godwin was a late addition to the injury report due to being under the weather. However, the veteran receiver will be active for the all-important divisional matchup with the Panthers.

news.head: Kaleb Johnson traded to Packers
news.body: Kaleb Johnson is being traded to the Green Bay Packers by the Pittsburgh Steelers according to Tom Pelissero.
news.impact: Details of the trade are still being finalized between the two organizations, with Johnson receiving the fresh start the running back desperately needs after falling out of favor in a Pittsburgh backfield that will be led by the duo of Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle this upcoming season. Johnson’s role should become clearer as the National Football League continues their investigation into No. 1 running back Josh Jacobs, potentially resulting in a backup opportunity behind current No. 2 option MarShawn Lloyd.

news.head: Kaleb Johnson given 'clean slate'
news.body: Steelers HC Mike McCarthy told reporters, “everybody has a clean slate and let’s get to work,” when asked about RB Kaleb Johnson.
news.impact: The former third-round pick had an extremely underwhelming rookie campaign, carrying the ball 28 times for 69 yards across 10 appearances. Entering 2026, he sits behind both Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle on the team’s depth chart. His path to fantasy relevance will be very difficult unless he stands out in training camp.

news.head: Kaleb Johnson officially inactive for Week 17
news.body: Steelers RB Kaleb Johnson is officially inactive for Week 17.
news.impact: Johnson was not listed on the injury report this week and will be a healthy inactive. Jaylen Warren and Kenneth Gainwell will serve as the primary running backs against Cleveland.

news.head: Kaleb Johnson active but logs no snaps Thursday
news.body: Kaleb Johnson was active for Thursday's 33-31 loss to the Bengals but did not play any offensive snaps.
news.impact: After receiving six carries in each of the previous two games, Johnson was held off the field entirely despite being active. Jaylen Warren dominated the backfield touches with a stellar performance, while Kenneth Gainwell also saw significant playing time. As long as Warren and Gainwell are healthy, opportunities will be scarce for Johnson, making him irrelevant in fantasy leagues.

news.head: Caleb Douglas leads pass-catchers in Week 1 loss to Raiders
news.body: Caleb Douglas caught five of his team-high seven targets for 94 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1.
news.impact: Douglas was the lone bright spot in an underwhelming Miami passing attack, leading the team in receptions and receiving yards in the loss. The wideout will look to provide quarterback Malik Willis with a reliable pass-catching option moving forward, with a Week 2 contest against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.head: Caleb Douglas set to start in Week 1
news.body: Caleb Douglas is set to be a starter for the Dolphins in their Week 1 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.impact: The Dolphins selected Douglas in the third round of this year's draft, but he had an impressive offseason for them and is set to be a starter for the team in their season opener. That's a great sign for his season outlook, as it means he will have ample opportunities to prove himself and break out from the very start of the season.

news.head: Caleb Douglas selected No. 75 by Miami Dolphins
news.body: The Miami Dolphins have selected WR Caleb Douglas with the No. 75 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.impact: Douglas heads to the Dolphins with the 75th overall pick after a productive career at Texas Tech. Douglas was a Second Team All-Big 12 selection last season after leading the Red Raiders in receiving yards (846). Douglas ran well at the combine (4.39 40-yard dash), but doesn't always showcase that speed to create separation vertically. He will have every opportunity to contribute immediately as the Dolphins have endured a major overhaul in the wide receiver room entering the 2026 season.

news.head: D'Andre Swift rushes for three touchdowns in Week 1 win over Panthers
news.body: D'Andre Swift carried the ball 18 times for 124 rushing yards and three touchdowns while also catching his lone target for 10 yards in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Swift led an impactful Chicago backfield attack in the season opener for head coach Ben Johnson, averaging 6.9 yards per carry in the win. The veteran running back will look to take advantage of another favorable matchup against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2 for fantasy managers.

news.head: D'Andre Swift agrees to three-year extension with Bears
news.body: D'Andre Swift and the Bears agreed to terms on a three year, $33.75 million extension with $27.5M in guaranteed money.
news.impact: The Bears continue to show their commitment to Swift, this time to the tune of a three year, $33.75 million extension right before the start of the regular season. This move dispels many of the concerns that Kyle Monangai would take over this backfield in the near future. Chicago continues to display high trust in their veteran running back, and he seems to be primed for a big year in 2026 so long as he can stay healthy.

news.head: D'Andre Swift (core) without injury designation for Sunday
news.body: D'Andre Swift (core) is without an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Swift will be able to play in the team's season opener on Sunday. He was recently battling through an issue with his core, but it's nothing more than a minor injury and shouldn't hinder him against the Panthers. He's expected to be a good fantasy option for as long as he can remain healthy and in the lineup for Chicago.

news.head: D'Andre Swift at practice Monday
news.body: D'Andre Swift was present at practice on Monday.
news.impact: Swift left practice early last week due to what was reported to be a cramp. His presence at practice on Monday is a good sign for his status heading into this week's season opener.

news.head: Bijan Robinson hauls in touchdown catch in Week 1
news.body: Bijan Robinson carried the ball 21 times for 83 yards and caught eight of his 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1.
news.impact: Robinson was basically the entire offense for the Falcons in the close loss to Pittsburgh. He scored the team's only touchdown on a 23-yard catch at the end of the first quarter. It was an excellent start to the season for the star running back, who will slot in as a high-end RB1 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Panthers.

news.head: Bijan Robinson agrees to three-year extension with Falcons
news.body: Bijan Robinson has agreed to a three-year, $75 million contract extension with the Atlanta Falcons according to Adam Schefter.
news.impact: The deal includes $51 million in guaranteed money while also making Robinson the highest-paid running back in the league. The third-year back finished with 2,298 total offensive yards and 11 total touchdowns in 2025 and remains in the argument as the 1.01 pick in upcoming fantasy drafts with offensive minded Kevin Stefanski being named the new head coach this offseason for the Falcons.

news.head: Bijan Robinson does not practice Wednesday amid contract talks with Falcons
news.body: Bijan Robinson did not practice on Wednesday amid contract talks with the Falcons.
news.impact: Jahmyr Gibbs did not practice either on Wednesday for the same reason. Both players are under contract for two more seasons and are looking for new contracts. They'll both be among the league's highest paid running backs with new deals and deservingly so. This will remain a situation to monitor, but it's too early in training camp to have any major concerns.

news.head: Bijan Robinson could land extension with Falcons this offseason
news.body: The Falcons are expected to prioritize Bijan Robinson for an extension this summer.
news.impact: This news comes after Atlanta extended Drake London on Tuesday. It is possible we see Bijan and Jahmyr Gibbs both break the running back market this offseason.

news.head: Harrison Butker perfect in win Monday
news.body: Harrison Butker went 4-for-4 on his extra-point attempts and made his lone field-goal attempt in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Butker did his job on Monday night, hitting all five of his kicks in the team's big win over the Broncos. He didn't end up with a good total from a fantasy perspective, but he should still be considered one of the better fantasy options at his position moving forward.

news.head: Harrison Butker perfect in Week 18 loss
news.body: Harrison Butker connected on 4-of-4 field goals in the Chiefs 14-12 loss to the Raiders.
news.impact: Butker connected on field goals from 36, 40, 41, and 47 to account for all of the scoring for the Chiefs Sunday. The veteran kicker remains under contract with the Chiefs for 2026 and should remain one of the top options at the position for fantasy managers.

news.head: Harrison Butker puts seven points on the board Thursday
news.body: Harrison Butker made both of his field-goal attempts and his only PAT in Thursday's 20-13 loss to the Broncos.
news.impact: Butker took advantage of all his opportunities Thursday, but he simply was not given too many. The veteran kicker has now made 29 of 34 FG attempts with a long of 59 yards over 16 games this season.

news.head: Harrison Butker connects on three field goals Sunday
news.body: Harrison Butker made 3-of-4 field goal attempts on Sunday.
news.impact: Butker made field goals from 54, 41 and 27 yards out. He missed one from 51 yards out. He is off the fantasy radar in the current state of the Chiefs offense.

news.head: Rashid Shaheed quiet in win Wednesday
news.body: Rashid Shaheed caught 1-of-3 targets for just four yards in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.impact: The speedy wideout wasn't able to do much on Wednesday, catching just one pass for four yards in the team's win over New England. The injury to starter Sam Darnold (hip) may have played a large role in his lack of production, however, so this isn't a good game to look at in order to discern his true involvement in this offense.

news.head: Rashid Shaheed agrees to three-year deal with Seattle
news.body: Rashid Shaheed has agreed to return to the Seahawks on a three-year, $51 million deal.
news.impact: Shaheed wasn’t what fantasy players hoped he would be in Seattle, managing only 15 receptions for 188 yards after being traded to Seattle despite his deep threat skillset and QB Sam Darnold’s deep throwing ability. However, Shaheed proved his worth in the return game, returning both a punt and kickoff for a touchdown for Seattle. Hopefully in 2026 he sees more work in the receiving game, as his price tag would imply. This likely means Tory Horton’s breakout is at best delayed, if not completely out of the cards with Cooper Kupp also still on the roster with Shaheed and Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

news.head: Rashid Shaheed testing free agency
news.body: WR Rashid Shaheed is expected to test free agency after failing to agree on an extension with the Seahawks.
news.impact: Shaheed’s value to the Seahawks largely came from his returning ability. If he signs elsewhere, he could become fantasy-relevant again.

news.head: Rashid Shaheed hopes to return to Seahawks
news.body: Rashid Shaheed, who ended up in Seattle from New Orleans at the trade deadline, hopes to return to the Pacific Northwest for a Super Bowl title defense in 2026.
news.impact: Shaheed was a game-changer for the Seahawks and their Super Bowl title run upon his arrival from New Orleans. Although he only caught 15 passes for 188 yards in nine regular season games with the Seahawks, he averaged 29.9 yards per kickoff return and 16.2 yards per punt return with two return touchdowns. He added three catches for 78 yards in three postseason games but kicked off the Seahawks' postseason run with a 95-yard kickoff return for a score on the first play in Seattle's Divisional Round win over the 49ers. Shaheed is a deep threat and a dynamic special teams player who should be on Seattle's list to attempt to work out a deal this offseason.

news.head: RJ Harvey totals 41 yards in loss Monday
news.body: RJ Harvey rushed the ball three times for 18 yards and caught four passes for 23 yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: The young running back was one of Denver's more effective offensive players on Monday night, which isn't saying much considering he finished with just 41 scoreless yards in the team's loss to the Chiefs. It looks like J.K. Dobbins will be the team's top rushing option this season, but it's encouraging to see Harvey's involvement in the passing game in Week 1, which is his path to relevance over the course of the season.

news.head: RJ Harvey (torn labrum) progressing in right direction
news.body: Broncos coach Sean Payton said the team is "pleased with how RJ Harvey is progressing."
news.impact: It was recently revealed that Harvey underwent offseason surgery to repair a torn labrum. He participated in 7-on-7 drills in practice on Wednesday.

news.head: RJ Harvey underwent offseason surgery to repair torn labrum
news.body: RJ Harvey reportedly underwent surgery this offseason to repair a torn labrum he suffered in the AFC Championship Game loss to the Patriots.
news.impact: This had not been previously reported. Harvey was able to do some work during Broncos OTAs. His status will need to continue to be monitored into training camp as he competes for touches with J.K. Dobbins and Jonah Coleman.

news.head: RJ Harvey inefficient in Week 18 win
news.body: RJ Harvey rushed the ball 15 times for 28 yards and caught 1-of-4 targets for five yards in Sunday's 19-3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: The rookie has been a good fantasy option over the last stretch of the regular season, but he had a bad season finale on Sunday. He was only able to rack up a measly 33 scoreless yards against the Chargers, despite seeing 19 opportunities over the course of the game. Any fantasy managers still playing in Week 18 were let down with his performance in this matchup.

news.head: Justin Jefferson scores two touchdowns Sunday
news.body: Justin Jefferson caught 8-of-9 targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.impact: Despite Kyler Murray leaving in the first quarter with a concussion, Jefferson was still able to produce in a big way with Carson Wentz. He remains a locked and loaded high-end WR1.

news.head: Justin Jefferson restructures contract with Vikings
news.body: The Vikings restructured the contract of Justin Jefferson.
news.impact: Minnesota is making moves to clear salary cap space. Pelissero notes they still have work to do to get under the cap by Wednesday.

news.head: Justin Jefferson goes over 100 receiving yards in Week 18
news.body: Justin Jefferson ended the 2025 season on a high note, catching eight passes for 101 yards in the Vikings' 16-3 win over the Packers on Sunday.
news.impact: With the 101 yards, Jefferson joined Mike Evans and Randy Moss as the only players in NFL history to record at least 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six seasons. It was, however, a bit of a down year for Jefferson, who finished with a career-low 1,048 yards and just two touchdowns. The 100-yard effort on Sunday was just his third of the season and his first since October 5. Jefferson was hurt by inconsistent quarterback play this season, but he still remains one of the best receivers in the NFL and should be a favorite to rebound in 2026.

news.head: Justin Jefferson hauls in four receptions in Week 17 win over Lions
news.body: Justin Jefferson hauled in four of his team-high five targets for 30 yards in the Vikings' 23-10 Week 17 win over the Lions.
news.impact: Jefferson has made the most of increased involvement in the Minnesota offense, recording four or more receptions in each of his last two games. The dynamic wideout will look to finish a frustrating season on a positive note in a Week 18 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.

news.head: Mike Washington Jr. sees seven touches in Week 1 win
news.body: Mike Washington Jr. carried the ball seven times for 41 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: Washington Jr. was impactful operating behind Ashton Jeanty in the Las Vegas backfield, averaging 5.9 yards per carry in the win. The running back will look to continue to offer impactful touches as the primary handcuff to Jeanty in the Las Vegas backfield moving forward, with a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.head: Mike Washington Jr. signs rookie deal with Raiders
news.body: The Raiders signed RB Mike Washington Jr. to his rookie contract.
news.impact: Washington was snagged by Las Vegas in round four this year. He impressed at the NFL Combine with his speed which he'll look to use to compliment Ashton Jeanty. Washington’s $5.36 million deal includes $1.1 million in guarantees.

news.head: Mike Washington Jr. selected No. 122 by Las Vegas Raiders
news.body: The Las Vegas Raiders have selected RB Mike Washington Jr. with the No. 122 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.impact: Washington is finally off the board early on Day 3. The big knock on him during his collegiate career was ball security, but he holds the speed and big play upside to have a chance of being an immediate difference maker. He will compete for a depth role in the Raiders backfield behind Ashton Jeanty.

news.head: Chase McLaughlin connects on five kicks Sunday
news.body: Chase McLaughlin made 2-of-2 field goal attempts and 3-of-3 extra point attempts on Sunday.
news.impact: McLaughlin connected on field goals from 34 and 51 yards out. He should remain a steady option for fantasy managers.

news.head: Chase McLaughlin makes 3-of-4 field goals in Week 18
news.body: Chase McLaughlin made 3-of-4 field goals and his lone extra point in Week 18 against the Panthers.
news.impact: McLaughlin had a field goal blocked late in the win. He finishes the season connecting on 32-of-38 field goals.

news.head: Chase McLaughlin has field goal blocked in loss
news.body: Chase McLaughlin converted one of his two field-goal attempts and both of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 20-17 loss to Miami. The veteran kicker had a 55-yard attempt blocked late in the second quarter—his first miss since Week 6—but later connected from 33 yards out.
news.impact: Through 16 games, McLaughlin is now 29-for-34 on field goals and 31-for-32 on PATs. He will look to bounce back in a critical Week 18 matchup against the Panthers.

news.head: Chase McLaughlin perfect in loss to Carolina
news.body: Chase McLaughlin made both of his field goal attempts and both PATs in this Buccaneers' 23-20 loss to Carolina on Sunday.
news.impact: McLaughlin was productive in the loss to Carolina and has been a model of consistency, scoring 8 kicking points in five of his last six games thanks to the offense's success. He should be a great start next week against Miami.

news.head: Kendrick Bourne hauls in eight passes Sunday
news.body: Kendrick Bourne caught all eight of his targets for 75 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.impact: Well, this was surprising. Bourne outpaced both Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson in Sunday's season opener, finishing just one reception behind TE Trey McBride for the team lead. This effort should make Bourne a popular waiver claim for Week 2, but the Cardinals are headed into a tough matchup against the defending Super Bowl champs.

news.head: Kendrick Bourne expected to see more snaps in slot
news.body: Kendrick Bourne is expected to see more playing time in the slot with the Cardinals.
news.impact: Bourne signed with Arizona in free agency this offseason. He is unlikely to hold much fantasy upside outside of a bye week fill-in behind Trey McBride, Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson in the passing game.

news.head: Kendrick Bourne signs two-year deal with Cardinals
news.body: The Cardinals agreed to terms with WR Kendrick Bourne on a two-year, $11.47 million contract.
news.impact: Bourne remains in the NFC West with Arizona. The deal has a max value of $16.47 million. He figures to step into a depth role in the Cardinals wide receiver room behind Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson.

news.head: Kendrick Bourne, Broncos expressing interest
news.body: The Broncos are expressing interest in free agent WR Kendrick Bourne.
news.impact: The market has been fairly quiet so far for Bourne. Denver is looking to add depth to its wide receiver room heading into next season.

news.head: Ashton Jeanty leads offense in Week 1 win over Dolphins
news.body: Ashton Jeanty carried the ball 23 times for 102 yards while also hauling in all six of his targets for a team-leading 45 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: Jeanty was dynamic out of the backfield in the season opener, leading the team in rushing and receiving yards in the win. the running back remains an elite RB1 option with PPR upside for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers ahead.

news.head: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) off injury report Sunday
news.body: Ashton Jeanty is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
news.impact: Jeanty practiced in full all week. He should be good to go in his lead role to open the season.

news.head: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) expected to play Sunday
news.body: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty is going to play in Week 1 against the Dolphins.
news.impact: Jeanty opened the week practicing in full on Wednesday as he works his way back from an ankle sprain. He remains a strong RB1 for fantasy managers going into the season.

news.head: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) practices in full Wednesday
news.body: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) practiced in a full capacity on Wednesday.
news.impact: It looks like Jeanty is strongly trending towards playing in Week 1, as he was able to put up a full session in Las Vegas' first practice of the week on Wednesday. If he is active, he will likely see enough work to be a great fantasy option in a positive matchup against the Dolphins.

news.head: Rico Dowdle quiet in Week 1 win
news.body: Rico Dowdle carried the ball eight times for 15 yards and caught two of his five targets for six yards in a 20-13 win over the Falcons in Week 1.
news.impact: Dowdle and Jaylen Warren split the backfield with Warren racking up more all-purpose yards (73 to 21) and seeing five more touches. Dowdle will continue to have fantasy value as he's proven in past years that he can be a difference-maker, but he should be on fantasy benches heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots.

news.head: Rico Dowdle, Jaylen Warren both see first-team reps Thursday
news.body: Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren split the first-team reps in practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Dowdle and Warren continue to rotate who sees the first reps with the first-team. They are likely to both be involved in a committee in the Steelers backfield this season.

news.head: Rico Dowdle signing with Steelers
news.body: Free agent running back Rico Dowdle is signing with the Pittsburgh Steelers according to multiple reports.
news.impact: Dowdle is coming off of a second consecutive 1,000-yard rushing season as he totaled 1,076 yards and a career-high six touchdowns with the Carolina Panthers. He finished four yards shy of surpassing his career-high of 1,079 yards in his final season with Dallas in 2024. Dowdle has played five seasons in the NFL and has carried the ball 567 times - but 471 of those have come in the last two seasons. He'll be the new running mate to Jaylen Warren in the Steelers' backfield in 2026.

news.head: Rico Dowdle linked to Commanders
news.body: The Commanders have been linked to free agent RB Rico Dowdle.
news.impact: Washington is likely to add in a running back this offseason, whether it be in free agency or the NFL Draft. Dowdle could end up being a fairly affordable option for them.

news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown hauls in 10 receptions in Week 1 win over Saints
news.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown hauled in 10 of his team-leading 14 targets for 67 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions' 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.impact: St. Brown was dynamic in the season-opening contest for head coach Dan Campbell, hauling in both of quarterback Jared Goff's touchdown passes in the win. The wideout remains an elite WR1 option in all formats ahead of a Week 2 road matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown has contract restructured by Lions
news.body: The Lions restructured the contract of WR Amon-Ra St. Brown.
news.impact: LT Penei Sewell also had his contract restructured. The Lions created $35.68 million in cap space.

news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown catches 11 passes in Week 18
news.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 11-of-15 targets for a game-high 139 yards in Detroit's Week 18 victory over the Bears.
news.impact: St. Brown closed out the year on a high note by registering his fifth 100-yard receiving effort of the season. It was also the second time this year that he caught more than 10 passes in a game. St. Brown remains one of the top receivers in the game and he closes out the year with 117 catches for 1,401 yards and 11 scores.

news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown (knee) active for Week 18
news.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown (knee) is active for Week 18 for the Detroit Lions against the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: St. Brown is good to go after passing through pregame tests on the injured knee without any issues, offering quarterback Jared Goff is most reliable pass-catching option against a tough Chicago defense in the season finale Sunday. The wideout remains a WR1 option in all formats.

news.head: Jonathan Taylor rushes for two touchdowns in Week 1 loss
news.body: Jonathan Taylor carried the ball 19 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns while also catching three of his four targets for 23 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
news.impact: Taylor was the lone bright spot in an underwhelming Colts offense to begin the season, averaging 5.2 yards per carry in the loss. The superstar running back will look to remain an impactful backfield option in Week 2 against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.head: Jonathan Taylor agrees to two-year, $44 million extension with Colts
news.body: Jonathan Taylor has agreed to a two-year, $44 million deal with the Indianapolis Colts that could be worth up to $47 million.
news.impact: The 27 year old is coming off of back-to-back 1,400 yard rushing seasons with at least 11 rushing touchdowns in each, including a ridiculous 18 rushing touchdowns in 2025. Taylor should be viewed as a top tier running back in 2026, and his deal secures his dynasty value for the next several seasons.

news.head: Jonathan Taylor struggles in Week 18
news.body: Jonathan Taylor ran for 26 yards on 14 carries in the Colts 38-30 loss against the Texans. He also caught 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards receiving.
news.impact: Taylor struggled to get anything going on the ground to close the season. It was a struggle over the second half of the year for him after he was the favorite to win Offensive Player of the Year during the first half of the season. He should remain a high-end RB1 heading into next season.

news.head: Jonathan Taylor finds the end zone Sunday
news.body: Jonathan Taylor ran for 70 yards and a touchdown on 21 carries in the Colts 23-17 loss against the Jaguars. He also caught 3-of-6 targets for 14 yards receiving.
news.impact: Taylor was able to salvage his day with a score on the ground. He also had another touchdown called back due to a penalty. It is unclear if he will see his usual role in Week 18 against the Texans.

news.head: Patriots D/ST allows 13 points in loss Wednesday
news.body: The Patriots' D/ST logged two sacks and allowed 13 points in Wednesday night's loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.impact: New England's defense got a lucky break with QB Sam Darnold (hip) leaving early on in the game. He was replaced by Drew Lock, and while the Patriots held Seattle's offense to just 13 points, that wasn't enough to lead them to a win. This unit should be a decent option against the Steelers in Week 2.

news.head: Patriots D/ST plays well in Week 18 win
news.body: The Patriots' D/ST logged four sacks, one interception, and one fumble recovery in Sunday's 38-10 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: New England's defense played well on Sunday. They held Miami to just ten points and made a few big plays to help out their offense. This unit has been great over the course of the season and will be a key factor in whether or not they will be able to make a deep push in the playoffs.

news.head: New England Patriots D/ST allows 10 points to Jets Sunday
news.body: The New England Patriots D/ST allowed 307 yards of total offense and only 10 points in a lopsided 42-10 win over the New York Jets on Sunday.
news.impact: The Patriots defense took a back seat to Drake Maye and the New England offense on Sunday. New England had just one sack and forced one turnover against the Jets, but the only real hiccup came on a 59-yard touchdown run by Breece Hall with the game already decided in the fourth quarter. New England closes out the regular season next Sunday against the Dolphins.

news.head: Patriots D/ST allows 24 points in win Sunday
news.body: The Patriots' D/ST logged two fumble recoveries and one sack while allowing 24 points in Sunday night's win over the Baltimore Ravens.
news.impact: New England's defense struggled for much of the game on Sunday, but they were able to step up in the fourth quarter, securing a big fumble recovery to seal the win over the Ravens. This unit projects to be very good over the last couple games of the season with matchups coming up against the Brady Cook-led Jets and the Quinn Ewers-led Dolphins.

news.head: Mike Gesicki explodes to open season
news.body: Mike Gesicki caught 5-of-7 targets for 78 yards with a touchdown in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
news.impact: While Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins were fairly quiet on Sunday, it was Gesicki who led the team in receiving. Despite his big Week 1 performance, he still isn't a reliable weekly start yet.

news.head: Mike Gesicki catches two passes in loss
news.body: Mike Gesicki caught both of his targets for 13 yards in the Bengals' 20-18 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
news.impact: Gesicki failed to get much going in this game with the passing attack of Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and Chase Brown taking most of the work. Between the trio of Gesicki, Drew Sample, and Noah Fant, there's just not enough to go around.

news.head: Mike Gesicki totals 47 yards Sunday
news.body: Mike Gesicki caught 2-of-2 targets for 47 yards in the Bengals 37-14 win over the Cardinals.
news.impact: Gesicki had a big catch of 32 yards. He will continue to split snaps with Noah Fant in Week 18 against the Browns.

news.head: Mike Gesicki hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.body: Mike Gesicki hauled in 3-of-4 targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 45-21 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: Gesicki had a pretty solid game against his former team on Sunday. He racked up 35 yards and a touchdown against the Dolphins, and Cincinnati was able to secure a 24-point win over them to put the cherry on top. He won't be fantasy relevant moving forward, however.

news.head: Lamar Jackson surpasses 300 passing yards in Week 1 win over Colts
news.body: Lamar Jackson completed 17-of-25 pass attempts for 324 yards and one touchdown while also rushing seven times for 40 yards, one touchdown, and one lost fumble in the Ravens' 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.impact: Jackson took advantage of a more explosive offensive playbook from first-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, accounting for touchdowns on the ground and through the air in the win. The superstar quarterback remains an elite QB1 option entering a Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

news.head: Lamar Jackson to play without contract extension to begin season
news.body: Lamar Jackson will play without a contract extension to begin the season for the Baltimore Ravens according to Mike Garafolo.
news.impact: Jackson is focused on football entering the 2026-27 season under a new Baltimore Ravens coaching staff, as the superstar quarterback is poised for another elite season behind center barring injury while also offering fantasy managers explosive production as a high-level QB1 in all formats with an intriguing Week 1 contest against the Indianapolis Colts ahead.

news.head: Lamar Jackson will not play in preseason opener
news.body: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson will not play in the preseason opener on Saturday against the Eagles.
news.impact: Minter said there will be some “established players” not playing Saturday. Jackson should see some reps in the second or third preseason game.

news.head: Lamar Jackson says he played through injuries most of last season
news.body: Lamar Jackson told reporters he played through injuries for much of last season.
news.impact: Jackson suffered a hamstring injury in Week 3 that got worse when he tried to make a move the following week in Kansas City. He wound up missing a few games, but he said he was still playing through injuries even when he returned.

news.head: Jason Myers scores seven points in win Wednesday
news.body: Jason Myers went 2-for-2 on his field-goal attempts and made his lone extra-point attempt in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.impact: Myers did his job on Wednesday, knocking in all three of his kicks en route to a win over the Patriots. He will likely be a decent fantasy option at the position over the course of the season, assuming QB Sam Darnold (hip) doesn't miss significant time and leave the offense weaker moving forward.

news.head: Jason Myers has rare off night Saturday
news.body: Jason Myers missed two field goal attempts on Saturday night but the Seahawks still managed a 13-3 win over San Francisco to clinch the top seed in the NFC.
news.impact: Myers had made 18 straight field goal attempts before his miss from 47 yards out early in the second quarter. He also missed on Seattle's last drive of the game when he hit the right upright from 26 yards away. Myers did have makes of 45 yards and 31 yards and also converted his only extra point attempt. Myers finishes with career highs in field goals made (41) and field goal attempts (48) while also converting a perfect 48-of-48 on PATs.

news.head: Jason Myers connects on five kicks Sunday
news.body: Jason Myers connected on both of his field goal attempts and all three extra point attempts on Sunday.
news.impact: Myers remains one of the top kickers in the NFL this season. He is 39-of-44 on field goals this year.

news.head: Jason Myers quiet in Seahawks OT win over Rams Thursday
news.body: After his historic six-field goal performance in Seattle's Week 15 win over the Colts, Jason Myers was not a factor in the Seahawks' 38-37 overtime win over the Rams on Thursday night. Myers did not attempt a field goal and converted both point after attempts in the Week 16 thriller.
news.impact: While Myers' performance could not have come at a worse time for fantasy owners vying for league titles, this was certainly a game script issue. With Seattle trailing 30-14 in the fourth quarter, the Seahawks could not afford to settle for field goals - or even PATs - during their rally. Myers was left on the sidelines as Seattle converted three straight two-point tries in the fourth quarter and OT. Myers entered having connected on at least three field goal attempts in six straight games and he still leads the NFL with 155 points. For those Myers owners fortunate enough to advance, expect him to bounce back in Week 17 against the Panthers.

news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs leads backfield attack in Week 1 win over Saints
news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs carried the ball 29 times for 156 yards and two touchdowns while also hauling in all five of his targets for 30 yards in the Lions' 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.impact: Gibbs was dynamic out of the backfield for head coach Dan Campbell, averaging 5.4 yards per carry in the win. The running back remains an explosive RB1 option in all formats, with a Week 2 road matchup against the Buffalo Bills up next.

news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs agrees to 3-year, $67.5 million deal with Lions
news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs has agreed to 3-year, $67.5 million deal with Lions that could be worth up to $75.75 million. Gibbs is now the NFL’s highest paid running back.
news.impact: Gibbs has done everything he needs to to earn this money. He’s a premier running back in the NFL, in the argument for the best. Now with David Montgomery gone, we will see how well he can shoulder a workhorse role, and fantasy managers are rightly expecting big things.

news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs does not practice Wednesday amid contract talks with Lions
news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs did not practice on Wednesday amid contract talks with the Lions.
news.impact: Gibbs has two years left on his rookie deal but is currently eligible for an extension. Gibbs could earn more than $20 million per year based on previous reports. This will remain a situation to monitor as Gibbs holds in to begin training camp.

news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs in position to 'reset running back market'
news.body: Jeremy Fowler reports that Jahmyr Gibbs is positioned to reset the running back market in a big way.
news.impact: Fowler expects Gibbs to earn at least $20 million per year when he lands a new deal. He had his fifth-year option exercised back in April.

news.head: Trevor Lawrence flawless in big win over Browns
news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 18-of-23 passes for 245 yards and four touchdowns in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns. He also ran twice for three yards.
news.impact: Lawrence played on easy mode against a Browns defense that just couldn't create stops. He had only five incompletions to four touchdowns on the day, a great ratio to have. With their win over the Browns, the Jags are the only AFC South team to clinch a win on Sunday. He faces a much tougher test against the Broncos next week.

news.head: Trevor Lawrence: Jaguars starters 'trending' towards playing Friday
news.body: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said he is “trending toward” playing the starters in Friday’s preseason game against the Panthers.
news.impact: The Jaguars starters did not see the field in last week's preseason opener. If they do play, it'll likely be in limited fashion.

news.head: Trevor Lawrence tosses three touchdowns in win
news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 22-of-30 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns in the Jaguars 41-7 win over the Titans. He also ran twice for 11 yards.
news.impact: Lawrence capped off a great season with a dominant performance against the lowly Titans. It wasn't always pretty, and there were plenty of struggles early on this season, but HC Liam Coen and Lawrence were able to get things rolling. The team is looking like they could be a tough out in the postseason, but time will tell.

news.head: Trevor Lawrence rushes for two touchdowns Sunday
news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 23-of-37 passes for 263 yards with one interception in the Jaguars 23-17 win over the Colts.
news.impact: The big part of Lawrences day was the two touchdowns he scored on the ground as a rusher. He continued his strong finish to the fantasy season during the playoffs the past few weeks. Lawrence should play in Week 18 with the Jaguars needing a win.

news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. finds the end zone Sunday
news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. ran for 40 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers. He did not catch his lone target.
news.impact: Jones was the 1B in the Vikings backfield behind Jordan Mason to open the season. He'll be a touchdown dependent RB2/flex play most weeks.

news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. joins Vikings on re-worked deal
news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. is returning to the Vikings on a one-year deal that lowered his base salary to $5.5 million.
news.impact: Jones’ return to Minnesota likely puts a damper on any potential flashy signing or draft pick the Vikings may have done otherwise. He should be a decent RB2 for the team, likely retaining the same role he has had the past two seasons.

news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. will be released or traded at start of league year
news.body: The Vikings have informed RB Aaron Jones Sr. that, barring a trade, he will be released at the start of the league year this month.
news.impact: The move will save the Vikings $7.75 million against the cap. That would leave Jordan Mason at the top of the depth chart in Minnesota for now, though they'll likely address the position in the NFL Draft.

news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. (hip) ruled out for Week 18
news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers.
news.impact: The season will be over for Jones. He totaled 548 yards and two touchdowns to go along with another 199 yards and a score through the air as a receiver.

news.head: Christian Watson scores two touchdowns in big day Sunday
news.body: Christian Watson caught 6-of-8 targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings on Sunday.
news.impact: Watson exploded for an 81-yard catch and run score early. He was later found in the end zone again by Jordan Love. He will be an upside WR2 next week against the Jets.

news.head: Christian Watson agrees to four-year, $110 million extension with Packers
news.body: Christian Watson has agreed to a four-year, $110 million extension with the Green Bay Packers. He is the second Green Bay receiver to sign an extension this offseason following Jayden Reed.
news.impact: Watson put together his best season on a per game basis in 2025 after coming back from an injury that forced him to miss the first seven weeks of the season. It’s quite a lot of money for a receiver who has been plagued with health issues and never had more than 620 receiving yards in a year. But to be fair to him, he averaged 13.2 PPR PPG in 2025 and he’s seen by many as a sleeper in 2026. This could certainly be the year he comes alive for the Packers offense.

news.head: Christian Watson does not see the field in Week 18
news.body: Christian Watson was dressed but did not see the field on Sunday during the Packers' 16-3 loss to Minnesota in the final week of the regular season.
news.impact: Watson, along with most of Green Bay's regular starters, did not play on Sunday. He finishes the regular season with 35 catches for 611 yards and six touchdowns in 10 games. He will be back in the starting lineup next weekend for the Wild Card round of the postseason.

news.head: Christian Watson goes for 113 yards in loss
news.body: Christian Watson caught five of six targets for 113 yards and a score in the Packers' 41-24 loss to the Ravens on Saturday.
news.impact: Watson led all Packers pass catchers in receptions, yards, and targets. It's his best game of the season to date and a nice bounce back after two down games. Overall, it looks like he's finally become the Packers' WR1, but we all know that can change quickly.

news.head: Jakobi Meyers snags touchdown in win
news.body: Jakobi Meyers caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns. He also ran once for two yards.
news.impact: Meyers didn't see a lot of targets, just two to be exact, but he made them count. Trevor Lawrence only threw the ball 21 times today, not counting throwaways, and ten different players received a target, so there wasn't much to go around. Hopefully Meyers will see more targets next week against Denver in what should be a more competitive game script.

news.head: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) good to go for Sunday
news.body: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns.
news.impact: As expected, Meyers carries no injury designation ahead of Sunday's season opener and will be available to play against the Browns. His presence is further competition for Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. in a crowded Jacksonville WR room.

news.head: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) limited again Thursday
news.body: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
