The second-year WR finished with his third-highest catch and yardage totals of the season. He finishes with 40 receptions and 475 yards over 16 games for the campaign.

news.head: Greg Dulcich catches two passes in Week 1
news.body: Greg Dulcich caught both of his targets for 18 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1.
news.impact: Dulcich was more of an afterthought in the Miami passing attack, finishing fourth on the team in receptions in the loss. The tight end remains difficult to trust as part of a Miami passing attack with more questions than answers to begin the season, with a Week 2 contest against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.head: Greg Dulcich nursing minor injury, return likely next week
news.body: Greg Dulcich is nursing a minor injury that is not expected to keep him out long. Miami HC Jeff Hafley expects the tight end to return next week for joint practice with the Commanders.
news.impact: It’s never great when a player misses time due to injury during training camp, especially on a team where potential target shares are so up in the air and building chemistry is essential. However, it doesn’t sound like it will be a long absence, so Dulcich should be fine as a sleeper selection in fantasy drafts.

news.head: Greg Dulcich emerging as top weapon for Miami
news.body: Greg Dulcich is emerging as the “top Dolphins weapon” at this point of the offseason, beat reporter Omar Kelly noted after Dulcich made a one handed catch.
news.impact: Of course many things can change, but Dulcich has shown ability in previous years and started to come alive late last season. Dulcich could find himself a nice role in 2026 if he keeps progressing and showing rapport with new QB Malik Willis. It’s also notable that the new coaching staff comes from Green Bay, a system that utilized the tight end heavily. That could also work in Dulcich’s favor.

news.head: Greg Dulcich expected to take on bigger role in 2026 season
news.body: Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN believes Greg Dulcich “should figure heavily in Miami’s passing game in 2026.”
news.impact: Dulcich is currently the starting tight end in Miami after re-signing with them. Darren Waller remains a free agent and it doesn't appear that he will be returning. The Dolphins moves the rest of the offseason will have to be monitored to see if they bring in any more weapons, but he could be in line for close to an every down role as everything stands right now. He can be a TE2 with TE1 upside for fantasy managers who wait on the position.

news.head: Chig Okonkwo quiet in Week 1 loss
news.body: Chig Okonkwo caught two of his three targets for 16 yards in the Commanders’ 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 1.
news.impact: Okonkwo was one of many underwhelming pass-catchers in a Washington passing attack that left plenty to be desired in the season-opening loss. The tight end will look to get back on track against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 2.

news.head: Chig Okonkwo draws praise as both receiver and blocker from GM
news.body: Commanders GM Adam Peters called Chig Okonkwo a "really good receiver" but adds he's super tough as a blocker.
news.impact: "He provides a lot of versatility with where he can line up," Peters said. Okonkwo signed with Washington in free agency this offseason. He'll be an intriguing double-digit round target for fantasy managers this season at the tight end position.

news.head: Chig Okonkwo: Commanders expected to involve TE's more in passing game
news.body: John Keim of ESPN believes the Commanders are expected to involve tight ends more in the passing game this season.
news.impact: Chig Okonkwo is expected to lead the Commanders tight end room this season. He will be a tight end sleeper to monitor in the double-digit rounds of drafts this year.

news.head: Chig Okonkwo agrees to three year deal with Commanders
news.body: Chig Okonkwo has agreed to a three year deal with the Washington Commanders.
news.impact: Chig is coming off of a career best 56 receptions for 560 yards in 2025 on the inept Titans offense, leading the team in both categories. It’s a good deal for Washington who bolster their receiving room with Zach Ertz no longer in town and Ben Sinnott as their current top TE, who has yet to produce in his NFL career. He should slide in as a top option for QB Jayden Daniels. As for the Titans, this paves the way for Gunner Helm to get his crack at the starting job, provided the Titans don’t replace him.

news.head: Antonio Williams leads pass-catchers in Week 1 loss to Eagles
news.body: Antonio Williams hauled in each of his four targets for 64 yards and one touchdown in the Commanders’ 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 1.
news.impact: Williams impressed in his regular season debut, leading the team in receptions, receiving yards, and yards per reception in a losing effort. The rookie pass-catcher will look to replicate his performance as part of a crowded wide receiver room alongside Stefon Diggs and Terry McLaurin against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 2.

news.head: Antonio Williams selected No. 71 by Washington Commanders
news.body: The Washington Comnmanders have selected WR Antonio Williams with the No. 71 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.impact: Williams led Clemson in receptions in each of the past two seasons. He showed good burst and acceleration off the line of scrimmage and has an ability to produce on gadget plays and screens. The slot receiver has good speed, but is not a true vertical threat and did have some issues with drops during his collegiate career. Williams, an excellent route runner, scored 21 career touchdowns and he should provide an immediate impact for the Commanders with no true number two receiver behind 31-year-old Terry McLaurin.

news.head: David Njoku grabs five passes in Chargers debut
news.body: David Njokue caught all five of his targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.impact: Coming into the season, many were curious to see how Chargers QB Justin Herbert would split the TE targets between newly acquired veteran David Njoku and second-year Syracuse product Oronde Gadsden. Njoku ended up with a 5-2 edge in passes thrown his way, but Gadsden came up with the biggest play of the day for the Chargers with a 26-yard gain. Still, it was a solid showing for Njoku in his first NFL game wearing anything other than a Browns' uniform. The 10th-year vet will remain a matchup-based streamer with limited upside for standard leagues.

news.head: David Njoku agrees to terms with Chargers
news.body: TE David Njoku has agreed to a one-year deal, worth up to $8 million, with the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: Njoku was a first-round pick by the Browns back in 2017 and ended up spending nine seasons in Cleveland. He earned Pro Bowl honors in 2023 after posting career-highs in receptions (81), receiving yards (882), and touchdowns (6). He has dealt with some injury issues over the last two seasons, missing a combined 11 games in 2024 and 2025. He did, however, still manage to catch 97 passes for 798 yards and nine scores over 23 contests during that time. With a quarterback situation that was in a constant state of flux in Cleveland, Njoku hauled in 384 passes for 4,062 yards and 34 touchdowns in his Browns' career. Now, he will have Justin Herbert throwing him the football, but will have to compete with Oronde Gadsden II, who had a great rookie season in 2025, for targets at the tight end spot.

news.head: David Njoku to visit Chargers Monday
news.body: Free agent TE David Njoku will visit with the Chargers Monday.
news.impact: The market for Njoku has seemingly been quiet as he remains a free agent following the NFL Draft. If he lands with the Chargers, he could impact the growth of Oronde Gadsden. He'll remain a player to monitor as he likely looks to sign with a team soon.

news.head: David Njoku visits Ravens Tuesday
news.body: Free agent TE David Njoku visited the Ravens on Tuesday.
news.impact: Njoku was released by the Browns earlier in March where he spent the first nine seasons of his career. Baltimore is seeking a new tight end following the departure of Isaiah Likely. It wouldn't be the most ideal landing spot for Njoku from a fantasy football perspective with Mark Andrews still in town.

news.head: Chris Brooks sees seven carries Sunday
news.body: Chris Brooks ran for 29 yards on seven carries in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings on Sunday. He did not catch his lone target.
news.impact: Brooks was the RB2 for Green Bay to open the season behind MarShawn Lloyd. He remains off the fantasy radar for now.

news.head: Chris Brooks placed on NFI list
news.body: The Packers placed RB Chris Brooks on the non-football injury list.
news.impact: Brooks can be activated at any point during training camp.

news.head: Chris Brooks takes first-team reps in 11-on-11 drills Wednesday
news.body: Packers RB Chris Brooks took first-team reps to begin 11-on-11 drills at OTAs on Wednesday.
news.impact: Brooks got the opportunity with MarShawn Lloyd sitting out team drills. Brooks signed a two-year deal with Green Bay earlier in the offseason. Pierre Strong saw reps behind Brooks on Wednesday as Josh Jacobs remains away from the team.

news.head: Chris Brooks agrees to two-year deal with Packers
news.body: The Packers and RB Chris Brooks have agreed to terms on a two-year deal worth $4.85 million.
news.impact: Green Bay was able to avoid putting a $3.5 million one-year tender on Brooks. He'll remain in a depth role in the Packers backfield.

news.head: Terrance Ferguson quiet in loss to 49ers
news.body: Terrance Ferguson failed to catch his lone target in the Rams' 27-7 blowout loss to the 49ers.
news.impact: The hopeful breakout for Ferguson came to a screeching halt on Thursday, with the tight end failing to garner a target until late in the game, and failing to bring it in at that. However, the entire Rams offense was dysfunctional; no one had a great day for fantasy aside from maybe Kyren Williams and Puka Nacua, depending on your criteria. And second, Ferguson was present on most of the snaps when the starters were in, a big increase from his part time role in 2025. Hopefully, with his snaps now increased, the targets will come. We may just have to wait a week for the Rams to figure out what happened to them and get back on track.

news.head: Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) off injury report for Divisional Round
news.body: Terrance Ferguson is off the injury report for Sunday's Divisional Round game against the Bears.
news.impact: Ferguson is set to return after practicing in full all week. He'll return in his 13 personnel role with the Rams offense.

news.head: Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) practices fully Thursday
news.body: Los Angeles Rams tight end Terrance Ferguson was a full participant in practice on Thursday ahead of the Divisional Round matchup with the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: Ferguson logged consecutive full participations, a strong sign of his ability to play against Chicago. There was previously optimism for his status, and an official designation will be given on Friday.

news.head: Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) 'optimistic' for Divisional Round
news.body: Rams coach Sean McVay was “optimistic” that TE Terrance Ferguson will play in the Divisional Round.
news.impact: Ferguson remained sidelined in the team's Wild Card win over the Panthers. He was starting to earn more snaps late in the season prior to his injury.

news.head: Darren Waller catches two passes in Week 1 loss
news.body: Darren Waller caught both of his targets for 28 yards in the Panthers' 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 1.
news.impact: Waller made the most of his minimal involvement in a Carolina passing attack that saw the ball spread to seven different receivers in the season opener, averaging 14.0 yards per reception in the loss. The tight end will look for more involvement in a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

news.head: Darren Waller yet to be cleared for Week 1
news.body: Darren Waller has yet to be cleared for Week 1 for the Carolina Panthers according to Steve Reed.
news.impact: Waller has practiced consistently throughout the week and is “good to go” according to head coach Dave Canales, but still needs to to be placed on the active roster ahead of Sunday’s matchup with the Chicago Bears.

news.head: Darren Waller practices Monday
news.body: Panthers TE Darren Waller practiced on Monday.
news.impact: Waller was seen catching passes from Bryce Young. It is unclear if he will play in Week 1 after signing with Carolina late in training camp.

news.head: Darren Waller signs 1-year deal with Panthers
news.body: Darren Waller has agreed to a 1-year contract with the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Waller will join the Carolina offense after coming out of retirement to play nine games with the Dolphins last season. Tommy Tremble and Ja'Tavion Sanders had headlined the Carolina tight end room, so Waller could see significant playing time if he stays healthy and finds a connection with Bryce Young.

news.head: Jack Bech finds end zone in Week 1 win
news.body: Jack Bech caught three of his four targets for 23 yards and one touchdown in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: Bech capitalized on modest involvement in the Las Vegas passing attack in the season opener, catching one of the three touchdowns thrown by veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins. The wideout will look for more impactful output as the season continues, with a Week 2 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.head: Jack Bech held without a reception in Week 18
news.body: Jack Bech was held without a reception on two targets in the Raiders 14-12 win over the Chiefs.
news.impact: Bech's season will end with 224 yards on 20 receptions this season. With a potential improvement at the quarterback position in the offseason, Bech will look to carve out a role prior to the 2026 season.

news.head: Jack Bech (back) officially inactive for Week 17
news.body: Raiders WR Jack Bech (back) is officially inactive for Week 17.
news.impact: Bech was listed as questionable to play against the Giants. Bech has not been a major factor in the Raiders' offense this season.

news.head: Jack Bech (back) listed questionable for Week 17
news.body: Jack Bech has been listed as questionable for Week 17 against the Giants.
news.impact: Bech has not played a big role in his rookie season. He remains off the fantasy radar.

news.head: Ted Hurst III catches three passes Sunday
news.body: Ted Hurst III caught 3-of-3 targets for 36 yards in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss on Sunday against the Bengals.
news.impact: Hurst saw more opportunity as the WR3 with Jalen McMillan sidelined and he was able to flash. He'll still remain off the fantasy radar heading into Week 2.

news.head: Ted Hurst selected No. 84 by Tampa Bay Buccaneers
news.body: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have selected WR Ted Hurst with the No. 84 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.impact: Hurst will add some size to the Bucs wide receiver room following the departure of Mike Evans. He showed the ability at Georgia State to be able to win 50/50 balls thrown his way. He could have an immediate role as a deep threat in Tampa Bay.

news.head: Chris Bell catches one pass in Week 1 loss
news.body: Chris Bell caught one of his two targets for 25 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1.
news.impact: Bell made the most of minimal involvement in an underwhelming Miami air attack, highlighted by a 25-yard reception in the loss. The wideout remains difficult to trust as part of a Miami offense still establishing their identity under new head coach Jeff Hafley, with a Week 2 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.head: Chris Bell (knee) will start Sunday, set to have no snap count
news.body: Chris Bell (knee) will be a starter and have no snap count in Miami's season opener against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday.
news.impact: The rookie fell in the NFL Draft this year due to a major knee injury that he was rehabbing, but it looks like he is 100% healthy heading into the team's season opener, as they confirmed that he will start and will not have a snap count in Week 1. He will start alongside fellow rookie Caleb Douglas, and it looks likely that one or both of them will become fantasy relevant this year with how thin Miami's WR depth chart is heading into Week 1.

news.head: Chris Bell (knee) activated from NFI list
news.body: The Dolphins activated WR Chris Bell from the non-football injury list.
news.impact: Bell has been recovering from a torn ACL he suffered last season at Louisville. He'll slowly be eased back into training camp with Miami.

news.head: Chris Bell (knee) 'long ways' from returning
news.body: Dolphins OC Bobby Slowik labeled Chris Bell as “still a long ways away.”
news.impact: Bell opened training camp on the non-football injury list. He is working his way back from a torn ACL.

news.head: Colby Parkinson hits pay dirt twice in Week 18
news.body: Colby Parkinson caught 4-of-7 targets for 36 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams 37-20 win over the Cardinals.
news.impact: Parkinson found the end zone twice in the second half of Sunday's regular season finale. Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will likely see the bulk of the playing time at tight end for the Rams in the playoffs.

news.head: Colby Parkinson snags six passes in loss
news.body: Colby Parkinson caught six of seven targets for 53 yards in the Rams 27-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday.
news.impact: Parkinson led the Rams in receptions, bouncing back after a dud Week 16 performance. He had a good run towards the end of the season and was the best Rams TE for fantasy, but it’s fair to wonder whether that will be the case next year with Terrance Ferguson waiting in the wings.

news.head: Colby Parkinson held to 21 yards in loss to Seahawks
news.body: Colby Parkinson was held in check during Thursday's overtime loss to Seattle, managing just 21 yards on two receptions despite Matthew Stafford throwing for over 450 yards. The veteran failed to make an impact against his former team, while rookie Terrance Ferguson commanded the red-zone usage to score the unit's lone touchdown.
news.impact: Parkinson failed to find the end zone after scoring in five of his previous seven contests, serving as a reminder of his low floor when he doesn't score. His path to fantasy relevance could become even more difficult in Week 17 against the Falcons if Tyler Higbee is able to return from his ankle injury.

news.head: Colby Parkinson hauls in two touchdowns in Week 15 win
news.body: Colby Parkinson hauled in five of his seven targets for 75 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ 41-34 Week 15 win over the Lions.
news.impact: Parkinson has maximized his role as a primary pass-catching option of late, catching at least one touchdown in five of his last six games. The tight end remains a stable option for fantasy managers in all formats ahead of a Week 16 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

news.head: Oronde Gadsden II hauls in two passes Sunday
news.body: Oronde Gadsden II caught both of his targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.impact: Gadsden was clearly the second option at TE behind newly acquired veteran David Njoku on Sunday. However, Gadsden did show off his big-play ability with a 26-yard gain in the second quarter. The hype was real around Gadsden for a time last season, but his fantasy value is capped with Njoku now firmly in the mix. Gadsden is a boom-or-bust option at the moment.

news.head: Oronde Gadsden II catches two passes Sunday
news.body: Oronde Gadsden II caught two passes for 23 yards in Sunday's 19-3 loss to the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: The rookie was active on Sunday but wasn't able to rack up a good fantasy total against the Broncos. He showed a lot of potential over the course of the regular season, however, which will likely make him an interesting upside option at the tight end position for the 2026 fantasy football season.

news.head: Oronde Gadsden II snags touchdown in loss
news.body: Oronde Gadsden II caught three of six targets for 32 yards and a score in the Chargers' 20-16 loss to Houston.
news.impact: Gadsden saved his fantasy day thanks to a one-yard touchdown pass from Justin Herbert as the Chargers were in comeback mode. He's now rotated between good games and single catch performances for the last month, showing some inconsistency, but that's not abnormal for a rookie tight end.

news.head: Oronde Gadsden II quiet Sunday
news.body: Oronde Gadsden II caught his lone target for seven yards in the Chargers 34-17 win over the Cowboys.
news.impact: Gadsden was able to get back on track last week after a stretch of limited production, which turned out to be the case for him this week. He is off the fantasy radar.

news.head: Jaylin Noel shows big-play ability on limited targets
news.body: Jaylin Noel hauled in both of his targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Noel only got two looks from C.J. Stroud on Sunday, but he had the longest gain of the day with a 35-yard pickup. The second-year receiver out of Iowa State has big-play potential every week, but he may not see enough volume to move beyond being a boom-or-bust fantasy option.

news.head: Jaylin Noel (hamstring/finger) returns to practice
news.body: Jaylin Noel returned to practice on Tuesday.
news.impact: Noel returns from hamstring and finger injuries. He is expected to hold a depth role in the Texans wide receiver room.

news.head: Jaylin Noel activated off of NFI list
news.body: Jaylin Noel has been activated off of the Texans NFI list.
news.impact: The young receiver has missed camp so far due to an undisclosed injury, opening the door for Jayden Higgins and Tank Dell to see additional work over him. However, he should work himself into the rotation, muddying things up for fantasy for the time being until we get further clarity on the pecking order.

news.head: Jaylin Noel (undisclosed) dealing with short-term injury
news.body: Jaylin Noel is dealing with a short-term, undisclosed injury.
news.impact: Noel was placed on the non-football injury list on Tuesday. It appears he won't miss too much time during training camp.

news.head: Samaje Perine totals eight touches Sunday
news.body: Samaje Perine ran for 20 yards on five carries in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers. He also caught 3-of-3 targets for 30 yards receiving.
news.impact: Perine was out-touched 21-8 by Chase Brown. He remains off the fantasy radar as long as Brown is healthy.

news.head: Samaje Perine sees 11 touches in loss
news.body: Samaje Perine ran 8 times for 42 yards and caught three of four targets for 10 yards in the Bengals' 20-18 loss to the Browns.
news.impact: Perine was a surprising name down the stretch that had flex appeal thanks to his rushing work, scoring three touchdowns in the final stretch of the season, as well as mixing into the passing game at times. He could retain some handcuff value in 2026 even as he enters his age 31 season.

news.head: Samaje Perine finds the end zone Sunday
news.body: Samaje Perine ran for five yards and a touchdown on three carries in the Bengals 37-14 win over the Cardinals. He also caught his lone target for eight yards receiving.
news.impact: Perine scored at the goal line in the blowout win for the Bengals. Chase Brown continues to dominate the touches in the backfield.

news.head: Samaje Perine scores once in blowout win Sunday
news.body: Samaje Perine rushed the ball seven times for 25 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 45-21 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: The veteran was able to take advantage of a great matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday. He totaled 41 yards on the day and was able to get into the end zone at one point, which left him with a solid fantasy total for the few teams that needed to start him. Chase Brown will continue to serve as the RB1 over the last couple games of the season, however.

news.head: Darnell Mooney quiet in win Sunday
news.body: Darnell Mooney caught two passes for 27 yards in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.impact: The veteran wideout had a quiet game in a win over the Cowboys. He contributed just 27 yards on two catches, which obviously didn't amount to much from a fantasy perspective. He isn't expected to be relevant moving forward, especially with rookie Malachi Fields there to compete for the WR2 spot behind Malik Nabers.

news.head: Darnell Mooney expected to be Giants lead slot receiver
news.body: Darnell Mooney is expected to be the Giants lead slot receiver in 2026, filling the void left by Wan’Dale Robinson.
news.impact: Mooney had a down year in Atlanta in 2025, but has shown the ability to be a capable target in the past and could be a nice value in drafts. Wan’Dale Robinson was peppered with targets each of the last two seasons (both with and without Malik Nabers), so this could lead to some nice stable PPR production for the veteran.

news.head: Darnell Mooney signs one-year deal with Giants
news.body: The Giants agreed to terms with WR Darnell Mooney on a one-year, $10 million contract.
news.impact: Mooney was recently released by the Falcons. He is a potential replacement for Wan'Dale Robinson in the slot for the Giants and adds another deep threat weapon for Jaxson Dart. He'll likely be in the WR3/WR4 territory for fantasy managers.

news.head: Darnell Mooney expected to be released by Falcons
news.body: Darnell Mooney is expected to be released by the Atlanta Falcons. The veteran wide receiver will count $18.4 million against the salary cap.
news.impact: Mooney had a solid first season with the Falcons in 2024 but then regressed substantially in 2025, finishing with just 32 catches for 443 yards and one score. He looked like a star in the making in his second season, catching 81 passes for 1,055 yards and four touchdowns with the Bears in 2021. But, he's finished with 40 catches or less in three of his last four seasons. Still just 28, Mooney still should have plenty in the tank and could be a solid pickup for teams with a shallow receiving corps.

news.head: Tyquan Thornton silent in win Monday
news.body: Tyquan Thornton failed to catch his single target in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Thornton showed a lot of promise in Kansas City's offense last year, but he is off to a rough start in 2026, being held without a catch in the team's first game of the season. He may get more involved as QB Patrick Mahomes II continues to knock the rust off after missing significant time with a knee injury, but fantasy managers shouldn't count on him being a consistent contributor at any point this season.

news.head: Tyquan Thornton suffers hamstring strain
news.body: Chiefs WR Tyquan Thornton suffered a hamstring strain at practice on Tuesday.
news.impact: Thornton was carted off the field during practice with the injury. It is unclear how long he'll be sidelined for.

news.head: Tyquan Thornton carted off practice field on Tuesday
news.body: Tyquan Thornton was carted off the practice field on Tuesday after spending time in the medical tent.
news.impact: It doesn’t look like Thornton was seriously injured, as he was riding in the front seat. His absence, if extended, could lead to additional opportunities for Cyrus Allen.

news.head: Tyquan Thornton re-signs with Chiefs on two-year deal
news.body: Wide receiver Tyquan Thornton is staying in Kansas City as he agreed to a two-year, $11 million contract to remain with the Chiefs. The deal maxes out at $14 million with incentives.
news.impact: The speedy wide receiver had his most productive season in the NFL last year, catching 19 passes for 438 yards and three touchdowns. His yardage and touchdown totals set new career-highs and he averaged 23.1 yards per reception. He also established himself as the primary kick returner in Kansas City and averaged 26.4 yards per attempt. Thornton spent his first three seasons in New England and has totaled 58 catches for 823 yards and five scores in his career. He'll likely assume a similar role next season, providing a deep threat on offense and serving as the kick returner on special teams.

news.head: Tyrone Tracy Jr. loses fumble in win Sunday
news.body: Tyrone Tracy Jr. rushed the ball two times for 14 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.impact: This year's preseason saw a lot of mistakes for Tracy, and that continued on Sunday night, when he lost a fumble despite seeing just two touches over the course of the night. He is clearly the RB3 behind Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary right now and will likely remain irrelevant moving forward.

news.head: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (personal) returns to practice Wednesday
news.body: Tyrone Tracy Jr. was back at Giants practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Tracy had been away due to personal reasons. He was back on Wednesday.

news.head: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (personal) absent from minicamp practice Tuesday
news.body: Tyrone Tracy Jr. was not at Tuesday’s practice for personal reasons.
news.impact: It is not an injury-related absence for Tracy.

news.head: Tyrone Tracy Jr. racks up over 150 yards of offense Sunday
news.body: Tyrone Tracy Jr. rushed for 103 yards on 18 carries, adding 56 yards and a touchdown on eight receptions in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Cowboys.
news.impact: Tracy ended his second NFL season on a strong note Sunday. His rushing and total yards were both new season highs. Tracy finishes the campaign with 740 rushing yards and 288 receiving yards over 15 games.

news.head: Kendre Miller reaches end zone in Week 1 loss
news.body: Kendre Miller carried the ball nine times for 30 yards and one touchdown in the Saints' 31-30 Week 1 loss to the Detroit Lions.
news.impact: Miller saw steady involvement as part of an underperforming New Orleans ground attack, tying for the team lead in carries on an otherwise forgettable day. The running back remains difficult to trust as part of a crowded New Orleans backfield once Alvin Kamara returns, with a Week 2 contest against the Baltimore Ravens up next.

news.head: Kendre Miller good to go for Week 1
news.body: Kendre Miller will be good to go for Week 1's matchup against the Detroit Lions.
news.impact: Miller is going to be good to go for the season opener on Sunday. His status was in question at one point due to some recent injuries that he's been dealing with, but he is over them now and will be fully good to go against the Lions. He will be primed for more work than usual if Alvin Kamara (knee) and Audric Estime (thigh) are both ruled out for this matchup.

news.head: Kendre Miller not seen at practice Wednesday
news.body: Kendre Miller was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
news.impact: Miller departed practice early on Tuesday. There will be an update on his injury status when available.

news.head: Kendre Miller (back) misses practice Thursday
news.body: Kendre Miller did not practice on Thursday.
news.impact: It appears to be a new knee injury for Miller early in training camp. Devin Neal and Audric Estime should only see more reps in his place.

news.head: Troy Franklin doesn't contribute in loss Monday
news.body: Troy Franklin failed to catch his lone target and had one rush for five yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: It was no surprise that Franklin was uninvolved for the Broncos on Monday night, as their offense struggled heavily to get even their best players the ball against the Chiefs. He seems to be squarely behind at least three other wideouts on the depth chart at this point, however, which makes him irrelevant from a fantasy perspective until further notice.

news.head: Troy Franklin (hamstring) listed questionable Sunday
news.body: Troy Franklin is listed as questionable for Sunday's AFC Championship game against the Patriots.
news.impact: Franklin was limited in practice all week. He should be on the favorable side of questionable. Pat Bryant cleared concussion protocol and is off the injury report.

news.head: Troy Franklin (hamstring) limited Wednesday
news.body: Broncos WR Troy Franklin was a limited participant on Wednesday ahead of the AFC Championship.
news.impact: Franklin sustained a hamstring injury in the Divisional Round against Buffalo. With Bo Nix out and Pat Bryant banged up, the Broncos are hopeful Franklin will be available.

news.head: Troy Franklin held catchless in Week 18 win
news.body: Troy Franklin did not haul in his lone target in Sunday's 19-3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: Franklin was not able to end the regular season strong on Sunday, as he failed to log even a single catch against the Chargers. He flashed some potential in the middle of this season, but if he is to have any fantasy value moving forward, he will need to get more consistent as a player.

news.head: Isaac TeSlaa sees one target in Week 1
news.body: Isaac TeSlaa failed to catch his only target in the Lions' 31-30 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 1.
news.impact: TeSlaa saw minimal involvement in the Detroit passing attack for head coach Dan Campbell, finishing tied for last on the team in targets in the win. The second-year wideout remains difficult to trust in all formats, with a Week 2 road contest against the Buffalo Bills up next.

news.head: Isaac TeSlaa continuing to trend in right direction
news.body: Lions coach Dan Campbell said he is “excited about where Isaac TeSlaa is trending.”
news.impact: Campbell added that TeSlaa has “looked like a consistent veteran this offseason." He was able to show flashes last season and appears locked in as the Lions WR3 heading into this year.

news.head: Isaac TeSlaa catches touchdown in Week 17 loss
news.body: Isaac TeSlaa caught three of his four targets for 49 yards and one touchdown in the Lions' 23-10 loss to the Vikings in Week 17.
news.impact: TeSlaa has had a nose for the end zone despite minimal involvement in the Detroit passing attack, hauling in one touchdown in four of his last five games. The rookie pass-catcher remains best left off rosters ahead of a Week 18 matchup against the Chicago Bears.

news.head: Isaac TeSlaa hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.body: Isaac TeSlaa caught 4-of-7 targets for 52 yards in the Lions 29-24 loss against the Steelers.
news.impact: TeSlaa hauled in an impressive touchdown in the red zone in the first half. It was his fifth touchdown catch of his rookie season.

news.head: Andrei Iosivas catches two passes Sunday
news.body: Andrei Iosivas caught 2-of-3 targets for 12 yards in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
news.impact: If you were told before Sunday that Iosivas was going to match Ja'Marr Chase in production, you likely would have expected a lot more. Iosivas remains off the fantasy radar as long as Chase and Tee Higgins are on the field.

news.head: Andrei Iosivas: Bengals could bring in competition for WR3
news.body: The Bengals reportedly could bring in WR3 competition for Andrei Iosivas this offseason.
news.impact: Iosivas is set to enter the final year of his rookie contract. This likely won't have a huge fantasy football impact on the Bengals offense as Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins continue to dominate the target share.

news.head: Andrei Iosivas catches four passes Sunday
news.body: Andrei Iosivas caught 4-of-6 targets for 41 yards in the Bengals 37-14 win over the Cardinals.
news.impact: Iosivas played a part in the big passing day for Joe Burrow. He remains off the fantasy radar heading into Week 18 against the Browns.

news.head: Andrei Iosivas catches one pass Sunday
news.body: Andrei Iosivas caught one pass for 21 yards in Sunday's 45-21 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: Iosivas wasn't a big contributor for the Bengals on Sunday. He was held to just one pass against the Dolphins, despite how efficient Cincinnati's passing game was over the course of the afternoon. He is not a relevant fantasy option at this point in the season.

news.head: Keon Coleman quiet in big win over Houston
news.body: Keon Coleman caught his only target for a yard in the Bills’ 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.impact: Coleman was very quiet in a game where Josh Allen threw for over 300 yards. He’s off of fantasy radars right now, and will need to show some signs of life before being brought back into fantasy lineups.

news.head: Keon Coleman (foot/toe) without injury designation for Sunday
news.body: Keon Coleman (foot/toe) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Houston Texans.
news.impact: Coleman's foot and toe injuries are no longer an issue for him and he carries no injury designation ahead of the team's season opener on Sunday. He isn't expected to be fantasy relevant for the foreseeable future, however.

news.head: Keon Coleman diagnosed with sprained foot/toe
news.body: Bills WR Keon Coleman was diagnosed with a sprained foot/toe in the team's preseason opener.
news.impact: Coleman was seen in a walking boot on Tuesday. Bills head coach indicated he didn’t have much concern.

news.head: Keon Coleman in walking boot, misses practice Tuesday
news.body: Keon Coleman did not practice Tuesday and was wearing a walking boot.
news.impact: It is unclear how serious the injury is for Coleman. There should be an update provided later in the week.

news.head: Kalif Raymond leads pass-catchers in Week 1 win over Panthers
news.body: Kalif Raymond hauled in eight of his team-leading nine targets for 84 yards in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Raymond made an immediate impact after rejoining his former offensive coordinator in the offseason, finishing first in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the win. The wideout remains one of many dynamic options in a crowded wide receiver room, with a Week 2 contest against the Minnesota Vikings up next.

news.head: Kalif Raymond signs with Bears
news.body: The Bears signed WR Kalif Raymond.
news.impact: Raymond remains in the NFC North after five seasons with the Lions. He will remain in a depth role in the Bears wide receiver room.

news.head: Kalif Raymond catches three passes in Week 18
news.body: Kalif Raymond caught three passes for 52 yards and added three punt returns for 33 yards in the Lions' win over the Bears in the final game of the season.
news.impact: Raymond established himself as another target for Jared Goff over the last five weeks of the regular season. After catching just 13 passes over his first 10 games of the year, Raymond caught at least one pass in each of his last five games and totaled 11 receptions during the stretch.

news.head: Kalif Raymond catches one pass in Week 17
news.body: Kalif Raymond caught one of his two targets for five yards in the Lions' 23-10 loss to the Vikings in Week 17.
news.impact: Raymond has struggled to make a consistent impact in the Detroit offense of late, finishing with two targets or less in five of his last seven games. The wideout is best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 18 contest against the Chicago Bears.

news.head: Elic Ayomanor finds the end zone in Week 1
news.body: Elic Ayomanor caught one of his three targets for an 11-yard touchdown in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
news.impact: Ayomanor was quiet for most of the afternoon until he pulled down his 11-yard touchdown in garbage time with 2:40 left in the game. The veteran wideout will be tough to trust as part of a below-average Tennessee passing attack going forward. The Titans will face the Eagles in Week 2.

news.head: Elic Ayomanor exits practice with shoulder injury Thursday
news.body: Elic Ayomanor left Thursday's practice early with a shoulder injury.
news.impact: Titans coach Robert Saleh added that Ayomanor is being evaluated. There should be an update on his status on Friday.

news.head: Elic Ayomanor puts up 50 yards in loss
news.body: Elic Ayomanor caught just 3 of 10 targets for 50 yards in the Titans' 41-7 loss to the Jaguars.
news.impact: Ayomanor got a nice, long reception during the Titans' first drive, but he and the rest of the offense were bottled up after that. Ayomanor ends his rookie season with 41 receptions for 515 yards and four touchdowns, but was plagued by drops, something he must clean up if he wants to earn a long-term role on the team.

news.head: Elic Ayomanor hits paydirt in Week 17
news.body: Elic Ayomanor caught 4 of 7 targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-26 loss to the Saints.
news.impact: Following a stretch of four games that saw him manage a total of just five receptions, Ayomanor now has seven grabs for 95 yards and a touchdown over the last two weeks. The rookie out of Stanford is having a solid finish to his first NFL season.

news.head: Xavier Hutchinson finishes with three grabs in Week 1
news.body: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-6 targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Hutchinson saw the third-most targets from C.J. Stroud on Sunday. The Texans are looking for a No. 2 wide receiver to emerge behind Nico Collins, and though Hutchinson's upside may be limited, he might be the guy at the moment. The fourth-year pro hauled in 35 passes for 428 yards and three scores over 17 games last season.

news.head: Xavier Hutchinson totals 84 yards in Week 18
news.body: Xavier Hutchinson caught 5-of-9 targets for 84 yards in the Texans 38-30 win over the Colts.
news.impact: Hutchinson led the Texans in receiving on the day with the starters sitting in the second half. He is unlikely to make a big impact in the playoffs.

news.head: Xavier Hutchinson shut out in Week 12
news.body: Xavier Hutchinson was not targeted in Thursday's 23-19 win over the Bills.
news.impact: Hutchinson was on the field for 21 offensive snaps and had a nine-yard run in the game, but he was not targeted in the passing game for the second time in the last three weeks. The third-year wide receiver has also turned in three games with at least three receptions during the last five weeks. Hutchinson has potential, but he is quite difficult to project for fantasy purposes due to this inconsistency. Notably, starting QB C.J. Stroud (concussion) is expected back for in Week 13, so do not close the door on Hutchinson completely.

news.head: Xavier Hutchinson catches three passes Sunday
news.body: Xavier Hutchinson brought down 3 of 5 targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 16-13 win over the Titans.
news.impact: Hutchinson did not see a single target in Week 10's comeback win over the Jaguars despite being on the field for 53% of the offensive snaps. He got back involved in Sunday's win, however, catching at least three passes for the third time in his last four games. Hutchinson does not have a lofty ceiling with his role in the Texans' offense, but he has some definite value in deeper fantasy leagues.

news.head: Jahan Dotson signs two-year deal with Falcons
news.body: The Falcons signed WR Jahan Dotson to a two-year contract worth $15 million.
news.impact: Dotson will have a chance to earn his way into the role held by Darnell Mooney. He had a limited role in Philadelphia behind AJ Brown and DeVonta Smith. He'll be a WR3 at best from a fantasy football perspective, but more likely in the WR4 range.

news.head: Jahan Dotson goes for 40 yards in Week 18
news.body: Jahan Dotson caught three of his eight targets for 40 yards in a 24-17 loss to the Commanders in Week 18.
news.impact: Dotson got some extra looks with the Eagles resting A.J. Brown in the final game of the regular season. The eight targets were a season-high for the veteran wideout. He will go back to a depth role in next week's home matchup against the 49ers in the Wild-Card round of the playoffs.

news.head: Jahan Dotson catches one pass in Week 13
news.body: Jahan Dotson caught one of his three targets for 12 yards in the Eagles' 24-15 loss to the Bears in Week 15.
news.impact: Dotson remains minimally involved in the Philadelphia offense, recording three targets or less in all 12 games. The wideout can remain off rosters in all formats until further notice, with a Week 14 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.head: Jahan Dotson sees one target Sunday
news.body: Jahan Dotson did not catch his lone target Sunday.
news.impact: Dotson remains off the fantasy radar in his current role with the Eagles.

news.head: Germie Bernard works with first-team in practice Saturday
news.body: Germie Bernard took first-team slot reps in practice on Saturday.
news.impact: Bernard impressed in his preseason debut with 51 yards on four receptions. DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. remained absent from practice on Saturday.

news.head: Germie Bernard sees reps with first-team offense Friday
news.body: Germie Bernard was taking reps with the first-team offense at Steelers training camp on Friday.
news.impact: Farbaugh notes that Bernard flexed into the backfield and then back out into the slot on a rep. He'll have a chance to compete for immediate snaps in the slot for Pittsburgh.

news.head: Germie Bernard draws praise from Steelers HC Mike McCarthy
news.body: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Germie Bernard was "crushing it" whenq asked about how he's handling playing all three positions.
news.impact: McCarthy had the same thing to say about Roman Wilson. "They're crushing it, frankly....it's best for our receivers to play all three positions to create opportunities for our receivers," he said. Bernard figures to move around his rookie season, but his best chance to more playing time could be in the slot.

news.head: Germie Bernard signs rookie deal with Steelers
news.body: The Steelers signed No. 47 overall pick WR Germie Bernard to a four-year contract.
news.impact: Bernard lands the deal on the first day of voluntary OTAs for Pittsburgh. He is expected to compete for an immediate role, potentially in the slot for the Steelers offense. He'll be a player worth monitoring heading into OTAs and training camp.

news.head: Kimani Vidal re-signs with Chargers on one-year deal
news.body: The Chargers re-signed exclusive rights free agent Kimani Vidal to a one-year deal.
news.impact: Vidal figures to remain in a backup role behind Omarion Hampton in the Chargers backfield heading into next season. He'll remain a handcuff for fantasy managers.

news.head: Kimani Vidal uninvolved in Week 18 loss
news.body: Kimani Vidal rushed the ball three times for 12 yards in Sunday's 19-3 loss to the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Vidal was cleared to play on Sunday after coming into the week with a neck issue of some kind. He didn't play much against the Broncos, however, touching the ball just four times in the team's loss. He will likely play a bigger role for them in the postseason, starting in a matchup against the Patriots next week.

news.head: Kimani Vidal (neck) officially active for Week 18
news.body: Chargers RB Kimani Vidal (neck) is officially active for Week 18.
news.impact: Vidal was considered questionable to play, but will suit up and lead the backfield with Omarion Hampton (ankle) ruled out. Hassan Haskins is expected to serve as the backup against Denver.

news.head: Kimani Vidal (neck) listed questionable for Week 18
news.body: Kimani Vidal is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
news.impact: Vidal would likely lead the backfield if he is cleared with Omarion Hampton (ankle) ruled out.

news.head: Kaytron Allen sees four carries in Week 1
news.body: Kaytron Allen rushed four times for 16 yards in the Commanders’ 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 1.
news.impact: Allen was more of an afterthought as part of the Washington backfield attack in the season opener, finishing last in touches in the loss. The running back is more of a change-of-pace option in a crowded Washington backfield at this point, with a Week 2 divisional contest against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

news.head: Kaytron Allen selected No. 187 by Wsahington Commanders
news.body: The Washington Commanders have selected RB Kaytron Allen with the No. 187 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.impact: The Washington Commanders entered the 2026 NFL Draft with a need at running back. While they missed out on Jeremiyah Love, the Commanders got a steal with Kaytron Allen in the sixth round. His 4,180 rushing yards at Penn State are the most in school history, ahead of several big-name stars, including Saquon Barkley. He will split the backfield work with last year's seventh-round pick, Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Allen could be this year's Kyle Monangai and potentially better for fantasy players.

news.head: Xavier Legette sees two targets in Week 1
news.body: Xavier Legette failed to catch either of his two targets in the Panthers' 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 1.
news.impact: Legette failed to capitalize on his minimal involvement in the Carolina passing attack, finishing tied for fifth in targets in the loss. The wideout remains difficult to trust in all formats ahead of a Week 2 contest against the Atlanta Falcons.

news.head: Xavier Legette (stinger) back at practice Sunday
news.body: Xavier Legette returned to practice at Panthers training camp on Sunday.
news.impact: Legette suffered the injury in practice on Tuesday. He will be competing for an immediate starting role in 3-WR sets.

news.head: Xavier Legette will not play in Hall of Fame game Thursday
news.body: Xavier Legette will not play in the Hall of Fame game on Thursday against the Cardinals.
news.impact: Legette left practice early on Tuesday, but he was cleared for a concussion. He did suffer a stinger.

news.head: Xavier Legette 'attacked the offseason'
news.body: Panthers GM Dan Morgan told reporters WR Xavier Legette "attacked the offseason."
news.impact: Legette lost his starting role in the middle of last season. Morgan said he is in a "great head space" and in "really great shape." He is likely to remain off the fantasy radar.

news.head: Jalen McMillan (knee) inactive for Week 1
news.body: Jalen McMillan (knee) is inactive for Week 1 for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers against the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.impact: McMillan will not suit up after being unable to clear through pregame activities due to the lingering knee injury, with Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin Jr, and Ted Hurst III to lead the Tampa Bay pass-catching group against the Bengals for head coach Todd Bowles.

news.head: Jalen McMillan (knee) doubtful for Week 1
news.body: Jalen McMillan (knee) is doubtful to play in Week 1 for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers against the Cincinnati Bengals according to Greg Auman.

news.head: Jalen McMillan (knee) practicing in full
news.body: Jalen McMillan (knee) was a full participant in Friday's practice session.
news.impact: After being limited by a knee issue on Thursday, McMillan showed no limitations on Friday. The third-year receiver is looking for a strong start after playing in only four games last season due to injury.

news.head: Jalen McMillan (knee) limited in practice Thursday
news.body: Jalen McMillan was a limited participant in practice on Thursday.
news.impact: McMillan has now been limited back-to-back days. He should be good to go on Sunday with another limited session on Friday.

news.head: Jaylen Wright sees one carry in Week 1
news.body: Jaylen Wright rushed once for a loss of one yard in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1.
news.impact: Wright was non-existent in the Miami ground attack, finishing behind De'Von Achane and Malik Willis in carries and rushing yards in the loss. The running back remains difficult to trust as part of a Miami offense looking for answers after Week 1, with the San Francisco 49ers up next in Week 2.

news.head: Jaylen Wright leads backfield in loss
news.body: Jaylen Wright ran 13 times for 23 yards in the Dolphins 38-10 loss to the Patriots on Sunday. He also caught both of his targets for 17 yards.
news.impact: Wright had a bunch of touches in this game, but failed to make the most of them. He’s the RB2 at best in Miami in 2026, but given his lack of production don’t be shocked if he is fully replaced by next season.

news.head: Jaylen Wright breaks off career-long run in win
news.body: Jaylen Wright made the most of his limited opportunities during Sunday's 20-17 victory over the Buccaneers, rushing five times for 56 yards. The backup running back highlighted his efficient performance with a 32-yard run, which stands as the longest carry of his two-year career.
news.impact: Wright has delivered significant late-season production behind starter De'Von Achane, having scored a touchdown in two of his previous three contests while eclipsing 100 yards in one of them. He could potentially see an expanded workload in the Week 18 regular-season finale against the Patriots if head coach Mike McDaniel chooses to reduce the snaps for his top players.

news.head: Jaylen Wright scores once in loss Sunday
news.body: Jaylen Wright rushed the ball nine times for 35 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 45-21 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.impact: Wright saw limited work on Sunday. He was able to rack up 35 yards and a touchdown on the ground, which helped out the Dolphins in real life but didn't lead to any particularly dominant fantasy total in most leagues. There's no reason to consider starting him over the last couple weeks of the season with De'Von Achane set to remain their bellcow back for the foreseeable future.

news.head: Najee Harris signs with Giants
news.body: The Giants are signing RB Najee Harris.
news.impact: Harris is working his way back from a torn Achilles suffered last season. He'll add depth in the backfield for the Giants behind Cam Skattebo.

news.head: Najee Harris visits Giants Monday
news.body: Free agent RB Najee Harris is visiting the Giants on Monday.
news.impact: Harris is working his way back from a torn Achilles suffered last season. He would add depth in the backfield for the Giants.

news.head: Najee Harris visits Raiders Friday
news.body: The Raiders hosted free agent RB Najee Harris for a visit on Friday.
news.impact: Harris went on his second visit after previously visiting the Seahawks. He is continuing to work his way back to full health coming off a torn Achilles.

news.head: Najee Harris to visit Raiders next week
news.body: Najee Harris is expected to meet with the Raiders next week.
news.impact: Harris visited the Seahawks earlier this week. He is working his way back from a torn Achilles he suffered last season. He is likely to serve in a depth role where ever he ends up.

news.head: Emanuel Wilson uninvolved in win Wednesday
news.body: Emanuel Wilson rushed the ball two times for three yards in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.impact: There were many questions about Seattle's backfield split over the course of the offseason, and we finally got some answers on Wednesday. One of the takeaways is that Wilson is not likely to be a significant contributor in the rotation, as he saw just two out of the team's 20 RB rushing attempts on the night. It looks like Jadarian Price and George Holani have squarely established themselves as the top two backs on this team, with Wilson being a distant third.

news.head: Emanuel Wilson (hamstring) off injury report Wednesday
news.body: Emanuel Wilson is off the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Seahawks.
news.impact: Wilson practiced in full all week. He'll be in a depth role in the Seahawks backfield going into the season.

news.head: Emanuel Wilson (hamstring) logs full practice Monday
news.body: Emanuel Wilson remained a full participant in practice on Monday.
news.impact: Wilson remains on track to be good to go for Wednesday’s season opener against the Patriots.

news.head: Emanuel Wilson (hamstring) practices in full Sunday
news.body: Emanuel Wilson was a full participant in practice on Sunday.
news.impact: Wilson enters the season in a depth role in the Seahawks backfield. He'll begin the year off the fantasy radar.

news.head: Cyrus Allen held catchless in win Monday
news.body: Cyrus Allen did not haul in his lone target in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: The rookie was silent in his NFL debut on Monday, being held without a catch in the team's big win over the Broncos. They didn't need to pass much in this matchup, so it's possible that he will improve and play better in closer games moving forward. Still, this was a discouraging debut from a utilization standpoint, and fantasy managers shouldn't have high expectations for him for the foreseeable future.

news.head: Cyrus Allen participates in 11-on-11s Monday
news.body: Cyrus Allen returned to participating in 11-on-11s on Monday.
news.impact: It was the first time in training camp both Allen and Rashee Rice participated in 11-on-11s on the same day.

news.head: Cyrus Allen (shin) back at practice on Friday
news.body: Cyrus Allen (shin) is back at practice on Friday, nearly a week after he suffered a bruised shin.
news.impact: Allen was the talk of Chiefs training camp this offseason, and now the team gets him back. He will look to crack the lineup and make some noise come go time, but for now he’s just a late round dart in deep leagues at best.

news.head: Cyrus Allen (shin) 'making improvements'
news.body: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said WR Cyrus Allen is "making improvements" from his injury.
news.impact: Allen remains sidelined with a shin injury. He began the week hopeful to return to practice by the end of this week.

news.head: Roman Wilson sees first-team reps Saturday
news.body: Roman Wilson saw reps with the Steelers first-team at practice on Saturday.
news.impact: Farabaugh notes that Wilson also took reps as a punt returner during practice. He is continuing to take on a larger role during training camp.

news.head: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) off injury report for Sunday
news.body: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
news.impact: The rookie was limited at practice earlier in the week due to a hamstring injury, but he is over it now and is off of the injury report ahead of Sunday's game. He isn't expected to be a strong fantasy option against the Steelers, however, especially with Cooper Rush set to start at QB for the Falcons in the absence of Tua Tagovailoa (oblique).

news.head: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) limited participant Thursday
news.body: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) was a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.impact: The rookie was once again left limited at practice. He's still recovering from a hamstring injury of some kind, and it remains unclear whether or not he will be ready to play in time for Week 1. Look for Jahan Dotson to see more work if Branch is unable to make his NFL debut on Sunday.

news.head: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) limited Wednesday
news.body: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: The rookie was limited at Atlanta's practice on Wednesday due to a minor hamstring injury that he's dealing with. It remains to be seen whether or not it will affect his availability for Week 1, but either way he isn't expected to be fantasy relevant for the time being.

news.head: Zachariah Branch ‘wired the right way’ per HC Stefanski
news.body: Zachariah Branch got some high praise from HC Kevin Stefanski, who said the rookie wideout is “wired the right way” and “somebody that really puts in the effort on a day-to-day basis.”
news.impact: Branch has made some highlight plays already in training camp, and with the No.2 receiver spot wide open, he’ll have every opportunity to impress and claim it. How he will be used in a Stefanski style offense will be interesting, as it doesn’t traditionally cater to Branch’s style of play, but that could change.

news.head: Bryce Lance catches three passes in Week 1
news.body: Bryce Lance caught three of his four targets for 42 yards in the Saints' 31-30 loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 1.
news.impact: Lance made the most of modest involvement in the New Orleans passing attack for head coach Kellen Moore, averaging 14.0 yards per reception in the loss. The rookie pass-catcher will look to carve out a larger role moving forward, with a week 2 contest against the Baltimore Ravens up next.

news.head: Bryce Lance signs rookie deal with Saints
news.body: The Saints signed WR Bryce Lance to his rookie contract.
news.impact: Lance was a fourth-round pick for New Orleans. He will compete for a depth role in its wide receiver room.

news.head: Bryce Lance selected No. 136 by New Orleans Saints
news.body: The New Orleans Saints have selected WR Bryce Lance with the No. 136 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.impact: The New Orleans Saints took Jordyn Tyson with their first-round pick, but the team lacked depth at wide recevier, leading to them selecting Bryce Lance. The former North Dakota State star is an excellent athlete and will give Tyler Shough a big downfield target to pair with Tyson and Chris Olave.

news.head: Raheim Sanders gets six touches in win
news.body: Raheim Sanders ran five times for 26 yards and caught his only target for seven yards in the Browns' 20-18 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
news.impact: Sanders played second fiddle to Dylan Sampson in this game, having exactly half the touches as Sampson. If the Browns retain him for 2026, he's likely the RB3 and will have little value other than as a handcuff.

news.head: Raheim Sanders quiet in Week 17 win
news.body: Raheim Sanders rushed for 21 yards on eight carries in the Browns 13-6 win over the Steelers. He caught 1-of-2 targets for 10 yards.
news.impact: Sanders split time with Dylan Sampson in the Browns' backfield Sunday. Neither should really be on the fantasy radar for those with matchups in Week 18. Sanders and the Browns will take on the Bengals in Week 18.

news.head: Raheim Sanders racks up 11 rush attempts against Buffalo
news.body: Raheim Sanders ran 11 times for 42 yards and caught his only target for four yards in the Browns' 23-20 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Sanders took over the majority of the rushing work after Quinshon Judkins exited with a broken leg. Assuming Dylan Sampson is not back for Week 17, Sanders could be an interesting flex option next week against Pittsburgh.

news.head: Raheim Sanders joins Cleveland
news.body: Raheim Sanders has been claimed off waivers by the Cleveland Browns
news.impact: Just a day after he was released by the Los Angeles Chargers, the Cleveland Browns have picked up the running back. The RB situation in Cleveland is fluid due to rookie Quinshon Judkins off-field issues. Dylan Sampson's name has been coming up as decent second option behind Jerome Ford so Sanders will be the perceived third fiddle for now.

news.head: Joshua Palmer snags touchdown in win over Houston
news.body: Joshua Palmer caught one of two targets for 34 yards and a score in the Bills’ 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.impact: Palmer’s fantasy day was saved by the touchdown, but unless you have him in bestball formats, it didn’t do your team much good. He’s the fifth best target at best in Buffalo right now, so it will be slim pickings with the roster currently healthy.

news.head: Joshua Palmer (ankle) questionable for Sunday
news.body: Joshua Palmer (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's playoff matchup with the Jaguars.
news.impact: Palmer was on the field for 84% of the Bills' offensive snaps in Week 18, but he managed just one catch on three targets for one yard. If Palmer does play, he seems highly unlikely to make much of an impact. The veteran WR finished the regular season with only 22 receptions over 12 games.

news.head: Joshua Palmer (ankle) officially active for Week 15
news.body: Bills WR Joshua Palmer (ankle) is officially active for Week 15.
news.impact: Palmer was considered questionable to play after being limited in practice to close out the week. With Gabe Davis inactive, Palmer should see WR3 looks against New England.

news.head: Joshua Palmer (ankle) to be questionable for Week 15
news.body: Joshua Palmer will be listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
news.impact: Palmer got in a limited practice to end the week on Friday. He should be on the favorable side of questionable heading into Sunday. He'll remain off the fantasy radar.

news.head: Demarcus Robinson catches long touchdown in win
news.body: Demarcus Robinson caught two of three targets for 50 yards and a score in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams on Thursday night.
news.impact: Robinson had a red zone target in this game as well, but failed to snag the short pass. His long touchdown saved his fantasy day, but it's worth asking: how many fantasy managers did it truly save?

news.head: Demarcus Robinson catches three passes Saturday night
news.body: Demarcus Robinson hauled in three passes for 24 yards during San Francisco's 13-3 loss to Seattle.
news.impact: Robinson tied a season-high with his three receptions while his four targets were tied for his second-most this season. He has now caught at least two passes in four straight games after catching at least two balls in four of his first 10 games of the year.

news.head: Demarcus Robinson catches two passes in Week 17
news.body: Demarcus Robinson caught both of his targets for 30 yards in the 49ers' 42-38 win over the Bears in Week 17.
news.impact: Robinson has seen minimal involvement in the San Francisco offense, recording two targets or less in each of his last six games. The wideout can be left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 18 contest against the Seattle Seahawks.

news.head: Demarcus Robinson hauls in a touchdown Monday
news.body: Demarcus Robinson caught both of his targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in Monday's win over the Colts.
news.impact: Roinson got the 49ers on the board Monday night, as he brought down Brock Purdy's first of five touchdown passes. Robinson did not do much after that, but he made his imprint on the contest. The veteran WR has not had more than two catches in any of his last five games.

news.head: C.J. Stroud plays well in Week 1 loss
news.body: C.J. Stroud connected on 26-of-38 passes for 274 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Stroud added 15 yards on a couple of carries and did not throw an interception in Sunday's season opener. He did lose a couple of fumbles, however, as the Texans took a loss in this Week 1 shootout. Still, this was an encouraging start for the third-year QB, and he's certainly at least going to be on the streaming radar for a Week 2 matchup with the Bengals.

news.head: C.J. Stroud, Texans pause extension talks
news.body: The Texans and QB C.J. Stroud will pause contract discussion until after the 2026 season.
news.impact: The two sides tried to come to an agreement on a deal before the season. Stroud will play out the final year of his rookie deal, minus the fifth-year option.

news.head: C.J. Stroud expected to play Thursday
news.body: C.J. Stroud is expected to play a few series in Thursday's preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.impact: Initial reports suggested that the Texans were going to rest their starters against the Raiders, but now they have made the decision to let some starters play a few series, including Stroud and the team's starters on the offensive line. He will be extremely limited in this game, so there's unlikely to be enough data to draw any fantasy conclusions from this preseason matchup.

news.head: C.J. Stroud, Texans starters not playing Thursday
news.body: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said the starters will not play on Thursday against the Raiders.
news.impact: Ryans feels he saw enough during Tuesday’s practice. They should see some reps in the third and final preseason game.

news.head: Carson Wentz tosses three touchdowns Sunday
news.body: Carson Wentz completed 12-of-19 passes for 133 yards and three touchdowns in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.impact: Wentz entered the game in the first quarter after Kyler Murray exited with a concussion and was ruled out. He connected twice with Justin Jefferson and once with TJ Hockenson in the end zone. He could be in the QB2 conversation next week in 2-QB and superflex leagues against the Bears.

news.head: Carson Wentz to serve as backup quarterback Week 1
news.body: Carson Wentz will serve as Minnesota's backup quarterback in Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers.
news.impact: Wentz beat out J.J. McCarthy for the backup quarterback job behind Kyler Murray for the team's season opener on Sunday. He found some success in his limited action as a backup last year, so him being next in line adds another layer of security for fantasy assets like Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison moving forward.

news.head: Carson Wentz re-signs with Vikings
news.body: The Vikings re-signed Carson Wentz to a one-year contract.
news.impact: Wentz had been linked to the Jets for a while, but it didn't end up happening. He figures to be the QB3 in the Vikings quarterback room behind Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy.

news.head: Carson Wentz unlikely to sign with Jets
news.body: The Jets are currently unlikely to sign QB Carson Wentz.
news.impact: Wentz had been linked to New York as a backup option behind Geno Smith. It is unclear who else might show interest in Wentz.

news.head: Jacoby Brissett leads the Cardinals to victory in Week 1
news.body: Jacoby Brissett completed 27-of-37 passes for 277 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.impact: Brissett was efficient and showed his typical veteran leadership in what most would call a season-opening upset of the Chargers. Brissett added 14 yards rushing on six carries, with a long of 11, giving him nearly 300 yards of total offense. The 11th-year veteran is coming off a career-best season, and he's now picked up right where he left off. Brissett could be a matchup-based streamer in standard leagues for the duration of the campaign.

news.head: Jacoby Brissett won't play Saturday
news.body: Jacoby Brissett won't play in Saturday's preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys.
news.impact: The veteran quarterback will not suit up on Saturday. He took part in the team's first preseason game, but they apparently don't feel that he needs more reps and will let him sit out of their next game. Gardner Minshew II is expected to be the starter with Carson Beck (ribs) unlikely to play as well.

news.head: Jacoby Brissett to work with starters in practice Tuesday
news.body: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Jacoby Brissett will work with the starters starting on Tuesday.
news.impact: Brissett returned to practice on Sunday after landing his new deal. The Cardinals are in pads for the first time on Tuesday.

news.head: Jacoby Brissett remains Cardinals Week 1 starter for now per Mike LaFleur
news.body: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Jacoby Brissett remains the team's Week 1 starter for now.
news.impact: Brissett agreed to a restructured contract on Sunday to give him more money for the upcoming season. The question will be how long he starts if the Cardinals get off to a rough start to the season.

news.head: Daniel Jones underwhelms in Week 1 loss to Ravens
news.body: Daniel Jones completed 19-of-31 pass attempts for 166 yards, one touchdown, and one interception while also rushing once for four yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
news.impact: Jones was unable to establish any rhythm against a disruptive Baltimore defensive front, totaling less than 170 passing yards in the loss. The signal-caller will be difficult to trust ahead of another tough matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2.

news.head: Daniel Jones will not play in preseason opener
news.body: Daniel Jones will not play in the Colts preseason opener.
news.impact: Jones has been fully cleared to return to practice. Anthony Richardson Sr. will start with Riley Leonard starting the second half.

news.head: Daniel Jones (Achilles) fully cleared heading into training camp
news.body: Daniel Jones is fully cleared from his torn Achilles and will be a "full go" to begin training camp.
news.impact: The Colts will begin their training camp on Tuesday, and Jones will be on the field participating in 11-on-11 play on day one. The quarterback suffered a torn Achilles last December and now looks to be on track to be ready to go for Week 1 of this upcoming season, barring any setbacks. Jones is still someone to monitor as the calendar turns to August.

news.head: Daniel Jones (Achilles) won't do 11-on-11 work in minicamp
news.body: The Colts say Daniel Jones won't do 11-on-11 work at minicamp.
news.impact: Jones was able to participate in 7-on-7 drills during OTAs. His status will need to continue to be monitored heading into training camp.

news.head: San Fransisco 49ers D/ST shuts down Rams in win
news.body: The San Fransisco 49ers D/ST shut down the Rams offense on Thursday, allowing just seven points in their 27-7 rout of the Super Bowl favorites.
news.impact: The Niners defensive totals were modest, with one interception and a fumble recovery, but were held without a sack. They just kept the Rams from moving the ball while not racking up much in the “counting stats” category. It’s a good showing for the team, and a date with the Dolphins is on tap. They are a great DST option this week if available.

news.head: San Francisco 49ers D/ST does nothing of note Saturday
news.body: The San Francisco 49ers D/ST could muster only two sacks and did not force a turnover during their 13-3 loss to Seattle on Saturday night.
news.impact: Yes, the 49ers only gave up 13 points. But, it could have been much worse as Jason Myers missed two field goals and the Seahawks failed to convert on fourth-and-goal on the game's first drive. Seattle had 361 net yards, including 180 on the ground, and did not turn the ball over against the 49ers defense. That's two straight weeks - and three of the last four - that San Francisco has not forced a turnover.

news.head: 49ers D/ST quiet in Week 17
news.body: The 49ers D/ST failed to register a sack or force a turnover in a 42-38 win over the Bears in Week 17.
news.impact: The unit struggled to keep the Bears from moving the ball, allowing multiple touchdowns on the ground as well as through the air in the win. The defense will look to get back on track in a Week 18 contest against the Seattle Seahawks.

news.head: 49ers D/ST forces two turnovers, scores on INT
news.body: The 49ers D/ST allowed 27 points on 312 yards of total offense, recording two sacks and forcing two turnovers in Monday's win over the Colts.
news.impact: With the offense lighting up the scoreboard for 48 points, the 49ers' defense did not have to do too much Monday night. The 49ers did come up with some big plays, however, including an interception that was returned for a TD as well as a fumble recovery on special teams. The 49ers D/ST has a tricky matchup coming against the Bears in Week 17.

news.head: Bengals D/ST forces four fumbles Sunday
news.body: The Bengals D/ST allowed 20 points on 282 total yards with four sacks and four fumble recoveries on Sunday against the Buccaneers.
news.impact: The Bengals defense forced three fumbles of Baker Mayfield alone on Sunday and one on Bucky Irving. They will face CJ Stroud and the Texans in Week 2.

news.head: Cincinnati Bengals D/ST rack up six sacks in loss
news.body: The Cincinnati Bengals D/ST racked up six sacks and a fumble recovery in the Bengals' 20-18 loss to the Browns.
news.impact: The Bengals defense started to show some life in the back half of the season, finally picking up some slack where they had been one of the worst, if not the worst, units in the league. They will look to bring in some help and improve around names like DJ Turner and Trey Hendrickson next season and get back in the playoffs.

news.head: Bengals D/ST impresses Sunday
news.body: The Bengals D/ST allowed 14 points on 233 total yards with four sacks on Sunday against the Cardinals.
news.impact: The Bengals had allowed just seven points until the final two minutes when Jacoby Brissett found Trey McBride for a garbage time touchdown. The Bengals will face the Browns in Week 18 to close the season.

news.head: Bengals D/ST logs two interceptions Sunday
news.body: The Bengals' D/ST logged two interceptions and a fumble recovery while allowing 21 points in Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: Cincinnati's defense logged three turnovers on Sunday, which helped to propel them to a blowout win over the Dolphins. This unit is not very strong, but they have a great end of season schedule with matchups against the Cardinals and Browns coming down the pipe.

news.head: Kirk Cousins offers mixed results in Week 1 win over Dolphins
news.body: Kirk Cousins completed 21-of-30 pass attempts for 160 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: Cousins was unable to find much success downfield, averaging just 7.6 yards per completion in the win. the veteran signal-caller will look to minimize turnovers moving forward, with a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.head: Kirk Cousins named Raiders Week 1 starter
news.body: Kirk Cousins has been named the Raiders Week 1 starter against the Dolphins.
news.impact: It’s long been presumed that the Raiders would start Cousins and give Mendoza at least a half-redshirt year. This just confirms it. He could be an interesting streaming option, but we need to see more from the pass catchers not named Brock Bowers to really feel confident in this passing offense.

news.head: Kirk Cousins: Starting job is 'his to lose' per HC Klint Kubiak
news.body: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said “it’s his job to lose” when asked about Kirk Cousins’ status as QB1 following Thursday’s preseason game.
news.impact: Cousins played on the opening drive on Thursday, which resulted in a touchdown pass to Michael Mayer. He remains highly likely to open the season as the starter for Las Vegas.

news.head: Kirk Cousins not practicing Saturday due to violating team rules
news.body: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak told reporters that QB Kirk Cousins is being held out of practice Saturday for violating team rules for fighting.
news.impact: Cousins and Maxx Crosby got into it during practice on Friday. They should be back on the field in the next day or two.

news.head: Panthers D/ST dismal in Week 1 loss
news.body: The Panthers D/ST forced one turnover (one fumble recovery) while also recording two sacks in a 59-37 Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: The unit did not have many answers for an explosive Chicago offense in the season opener, allowing eight total touchdowns on 592 offensive yards, with six of those scores coming on the ground in the loss. The unit will look to get back on track against an Atlanta Falcons offense that could be forced to once again start quarterback Cooper Rush in Week 2.

news.head: Panthers D/ST allows 16 points in Week 18
news.body: The Panthers D/ST allowed 16 points on 338 total yards with one interception and two sacks in Week 18 against the Buccaneers.
news.impact: Baker Mayfield drove the Bucs offense down the field for a touchdown on the opening drive of the game. Carolina made the necessary adjustments to keep the team in the game through the end. They will take on the Rams at home next weekend in the Wild Card round.

news.head: Carolina Panthers D/ST forces two turnovers Sunday
